- **Direct3D 11:**
  - `UpdateSubresource` on a staging buffer is ignored as on Windows (FIFA 23 stopped).
  - The swap chain answers `SetRotation` and `GetRotation`, so SDL2 games start (The Battle for Wesnoth).
  - A texture larger than Direct3D 11 allows is refused with an error the game can handle, instead of ending it (The Witness, Rise of the Tomb Raider, Transformers, Danganronpa).
- **Direct3D 12:**
  - Command bundles work (Kingdom Hearts HD 1.5+2.5 ReMIX's launcher).
  - Copy footprints of block-compressed textures come in whole blocks, as Windows reports them (Satisfactory and other Unreal Engine 5 games stopped at their first texture upload).
  - 64-bit texture atomics are used only on GPUs that have them; on A15, M1 and M2 the game no longer stops (REANIMAL).
  - A texture view of the other sample count, and a texture larger than the GPU allows, no longer end the game (Age of Wonders 4, Shadow of the Tomb Raider).
  - Fences answer `ID3D12Fence1` and heaps answer `ID3D12Heap1`, as on Windows; a game that created its fences or heaps through these interfaces took the refusal for an error (one showed "not enough system and video memory" at its start).
  - Resources, heaps, descriptor heaps, query heaps, fences, pipeline states, command allocators, command signatures and command queues answer `ID3D12Pageable`.
  - Shaders that read the result of a 64-bit texture atomic are converted.
  - A clear of a texture to zero through a view of another texel size is done, not skipped.
  - Many clear values in one frame are written exactly.
  - A shader the converter refuses is named in the log with the converter's message.
  - With the pipeline library switch on (`d3d12-pipeline-library = 1`), the shader cache capability also reports pipeline libraries.
- **Metal limits:** a texture larger than every Apple GPU supports is refused before Metal sees it, so the game gets an error instead of being ended.
- **HLSL compiler (shaders compiled while the game runs):**
  - `register(ps, c0)` and similar forms are accepted (S.T.A.L.K.E.R.: Clear Sky).
  - Six more Direct3D 9 words are read as names.
  - The Direct3D 10/11 compile helpers report their result as Windows does.
- **NVAPI** (with **Report an NVIDIA GPU** on): calls made with a null GPU handle now answer for the first GPU, as NVIDIA's driver does.
- **OpenGL:** auto-tune recognises more OpenGL-only games and turns BCD's OpenGL on for them (DOOM 64, Deponia, Into the Breach, Angry Birds, AppGameKit and Godot 4 games).

### Steam (BCD Dock)

- **"Steam is not running" (error 113) in 32-bit games:** Steam's entries are now also written where a 32-bit game reads them (Hitman: Blood Money, Bulletstorm, Medal of Honor: Airborne, LEGO Marvel Super Heroes).
- **Error 42 at the start:** missing Steam client entries are put back before each start (Terraria, Stardew Valley, Team Fortress 2, Grind Survivors).
- **A game that closes on its own** within 30 seconds without a picture now ends its session, whatever code it ends with (Black Mesa, The Binding of Isaac, Meccha Chameleon). Before, you had to close it yourself.
- **A starter that closes before its game** no longer takes Steam away from the game (Control).
- **Unsupported Steam client files:** Valve client files BCD Dock does not support are named. **Settings › BCD Dock › Valve's client files › Replace client components** puts supported ones in place; nothing is deleted.
- **Steam's refusals named:** "update required" (error 19) and "playing on another device" (error 35) are named on the starting screen and by auto-tune.
- **Copy protection (CEG):** the Steam client service is started again when it stops, and the log shows why a CEG job failed.
- **Install scripts:** Capcom's codec notice is no longer run (every Capcom game's first start only ran installs). The Paradox launcher gets Windows Installer (Prison Architect, Hearts of Iron IV).

### The app

- **JIT memory:** when StikDebug has been attached for a while or the phone is hot, the starting screen says before the request that the screen can freeze for up to 30 seconds. After 30 seconds without an answer it says how to start again. The box at the next start adds that StikDebug stops answering far more often on a hot phone.
- **Low Power Mode:** the starting screen says when it is on, because games and launchers then start and run much slower.
- **iPad:** a game's **Resolution** row says that a lower resolution (with MetalFX upscaling) is the first thing to try when a game stutters.
- **A game left in the background:** the crash box of a session that ran 90 seconds or more says to stay in BCD while the game runs, because iOS closes a large app that goes to the background.
- **Start over:** a game's page has **Start over with BCD's settings** under Recommended settings. A reset never touches the game's own files, saves or in-game options.
- **A copy that cannot run games:** a copy installed without the debugging right now shows "This copy can't run games yet" and the reason, instead of the setup pages.
- **Landscape lock:** a lock is applied again when BCD comes back from the background (a game showed in half the screen after returning).
- **Memory kills:** the text names the device's own memory limit and says when a game needs a device with more.

### Windows desktop

- **Close** and **Start › Shut Down** end the Windows desktop session.
- A program started from the desktop that has recommended settings gets a note that they apply when it is added as a game.

### Audio

- A game whose sound broke up in every frame (Quake II, Counter-Strike 2, Deadlock, Resonance, Dead Rising and others) gets a shorter audio buffer by itself.

### Memory and the emulator

- Thread contexts carry the vector registers, as on Windows.
- Two leaks of the emulator's code memory are closed.
- Each Windows module gets its own thread-local data slot (before, some shared the main program's).
- Freeing a thread-local slot no longer clears it in other programs of the session, as on Windows (Assassin's Creed).
- **No longer end the game or hang:**
  - Damaged relocation tables (Roommate, The Edge Of).
  - A 32-bit stack overflow, now reported as one.
  - A self-locking 32-bit start (FTL, Peggle Deluxe).
  - .NET services started from a 64-bit session (the Epic version of GTA V Enhanced, The Escapists).
  - Several x86 instruction forms with a REP prefix.
- Mono and Unity games whose code sits behind a .NET assembly no longer hang (the MZ view check is now on by default).
- A Unity game's garbage collector race is repaired in one more case (1000xRESIST).
- A crash inside BCD's own fault handling on a wild return address is gone (Maneater).
- Windowed games: taps, clicks and the pointer land in the game's window (Slime Rancher 2).

### Auto-tune

- A session that never drew a frame is no longer counted as played.
- A memory kill is recognised after a recovered GPU error.
- A game's block-compressed textures can trigger the texture size clamp before a swap file.
- A start where Wine never began is not scored.
- A player's own swap size is kept while the other swap lines are tried.
- A rule can say what to choose instead of "No setting changes this".
- Text written in a sent log's comment no longer counts as the game's.
- Over 150 new rules, among them those for the fixes above, 64-bit games that need an extra Windows DLL (Watch Dogs, DRAGON BALL FighterZ, Ghost of Tsushima, Momo Game, Football Manager 2020, Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced), protected games that need their registers kept (Football Manager 2024 and 27, Yakuza Kiwami 3, PRAGMATA, Metaphor: ReFantazio), Direct3D 8 games, memory kills and many known stops.
- A build number like `634.4` (a re-signed copy) is read as 634, so recommended settings with a minimum build apply.

### Recommended settings

**New:** Angry Birds, Arctic Drive Demo, Assassin's Creed: Brotherhood, Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced, Astro Tripper, Baba Is You, Battlefield 1942, BlueField, Brotato, Buckshot Roulette, Bulletstorm, Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, Call of Duty: World at War, Crash Bandicoot N. Sane Trilogy, Dark Deception: Chapter 1, Deponia: The Complete Journey, Dishonored, DmC: Devil May Cry, DOOM 64, DRAGON BALL FighterZ, Dying Light: The Beast, Eslabong, Far Cry 3 (outside Steam), Far Cry 4, FIFA 23, Fear & Hunger 2: Termina, Find The Needle Demo, Football Manager 2020, Football Manager (outside Steam), FreshWomen - Season 1, GP Bikes, Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, Half Sword Demo, Hearts of Iron IV, Inscryption, Into the Breach, Killer Instinct, L.A. Noire, Mafia, Metaphor: ReFantazio, Mirror's Edge, Momo Game, Need for Speed: Most Wanted (2012), Need for Speed: SHIFT, Noita, POLYBIUS, Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown, Quake II, REPLACED, Resonance, SC Jogos (Barro GT), Slime Rancher 2, Sonic Generations, The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion, THE KING OF FIGHTERS XIV, The Witcher 2, Watch Dogs, Yakuza Kiwami 3 & Dark Ties.

**Updated:** 1000xRESIST, Balatro, BioShock, Burnout Paradise: The Ultimate Box, Control, CrossCode, DARK SOULS III, DRAGON BALL: Sparking! ZERO, Dying Light, Fallout 3, Far Cry 3, Football Manager 27, Ghost of Tsushima, Halo: The Master Chief Collection, Hitman: Contracts, Just Cause 3, Max Payne 3, Mewgenics, Need for Speed: Underground 2, No More Room in Hell, Oxygen Not Included, PRAGMATA, Poppy Playtime, REANIMAL, Requiem: Avenging Angel, Resident Evil 5, Slay the Spire 2, The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth, The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, Ubisoft Connect.

### Logs

- **Error box code dump:** with `env.MADEIRA_DIALOG_CODE_DUMP = 1` (off by default), the log shows the game's own code that showed an error box.
- New lines name more failures:
  - A program's damaged relocation table.
  - A 32-bit program's huge reservation.
  - Long directory listings.
  - Failed opens of named objects (on request).
  - A refused HLSL shader's source (on request).
  - The first audible sound of a game.
  - GPU errors with their timing.
  - Steam's view of a game's start (Steam client entries, the game's own Steam check).
  - The Steam client's connection while a CEG job waits.

### Under the hood

Everything below is off by default unless a game's recommended settings or auto-tune turn it on.

- **Direct3D 12:**
  - `d3d12-device9`, `d3d12-fence-flags` (shared fence flags).
  - `dxil-target-latest` (convert shaders for the device's newest GPU family).
  - `dxil-loop-guard` (stop listed shaders' loops after 65,536 rounds instead of hanging the GPU).
  - `heap-backing` mode 2.
  - `trace-buffer-size` and `trace-dispatch` (diagnostics).
  - `d3d12-footprint-block-align = 0` turns this build's footprint change off.
- **Direct3D 9 and 11:** `env.MADEIRA_VIEW_PRIVATE_REF`, `env.DXMT_MODE_LIST_ANY_BPP`.
- **Vulkan:** `vulkan`, `env.MADEIRA_VULKAN_LIBRARY`, `env.MADEIRA_VK_HOST_SUBOPTIMAL`.
- **OpenGL:** `env.MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE`, `env.MESA_GLSL_VERSION_OVERRIDE`, `env.MADEIRA_GL_EMPTY_EXTENSIONS`.
- **Memory:**
  - `env.MADEIRA_BIG_HINT_EXACT` (modes 2 and 3).
  - `env.MADEIRA_JUMBO_HALF = 2`, `oversize-reserve-min-mb`, `oversize-reserve-eager`.
  - `env.MADEIRA_FEX_ARENA_REAP`, `env.MADEIRA_WOW_JUMBO_INSIDE`, `env.MADEIRA_X64_RWX_PLAIN`, `env.MADEIRA_GUEST_RWX_DATA = 2`.
  - `env.MADEIRA_ANON_POOL_ADJACENT`, `env.MADEIRA_COMMIT_GUARD_CLEAR`.
  - `env.MADEIRA_POOL_CARVE_MERGE`, `env.MADEIRA_POOL_CODE_FOREGROUND`, `env.MADEIRA_POOL_CODE_DEFER_FREE`, `env.MADEIRA_POOL_CODE_KEEP_BIG`.
  - `env.MADEIRA_X64_HOOK_ZONE`, `env.MADEIRA_SELF_WRITE`, `env.MADEIRA_KILL_REAP`.
- **Emulator and Wine:**
  - `env.MADEIRA_FEX_SPLIT_LOCK`, `env.FEX_SMCCHECKS`, `env.MADEIRA_CTX_FP`.
  - `env.MADEIRA_SLEEP_KERNEL_APC`, `env.MADEIRA_WOA_RECHECK`.
  - `env.MADEIRA_DNS_REFUSE_CRASH` (do not contact Valve's crash-report server).
  - `env.MADEIRA_DISPLAY_FOLLOW_BORDERLESS`.
- **Audio:** `env.MADEIRA_AUDIO_CAPTURE` (one silent recording device, never the microphone).
- **Steam (BCD Dock):**
  - `env.MADEIRA_DOCK_KEEP_ALIVE` (hold the session while a game's programs run).
  - `env.MADEIRA_ROCKSTAR_LOCAL_SERVICES`.
- **Diagnostics:** `env.MADEIRA_TLS_DIAG`, `env.MADEIRA_SEAM_TRACE`, `env.MADEIRA_FAULT_PEEK`, `env.MADEIRA_SPIN_DUMP_REGS`, `env.MADEIRA_STUCK_WAIT_DIAG`, `env.MADEIRA_EXIT_POOL_DIAG`, `env.MADEIRA_EXIT_POOL_SKIP`, `env.MADEIRA_HLSL_FAIL_DUMP`, `env.MADEIRA_OBJ_TRACE`, `env.MADEIRA_DIALOG_CODE_DUMP`, `env.MADEIRA_NVAPI_DEVICE_ID`.
- **More Windows DLLs that a game can ask for** in `env.MADEIRA_OPTIN_DLLS`: `msvcp_win`, `bluetoothapis`, `gameinput`, `ntdsapi`, `mfplay`, `avicap32`, `coremessaging`, `combase`, `dxdiagn`. Auto-tune can now add a second DLL to one it kept.
- **On by default, with a switch to turn them off:**
  - Each of these is a fix; `0` restores the old behaviour.
  - `env.MADEIRA_MZ_VIEW_CHECK`, `env.MADEIRA_TLS_CLEAR_OWN_PROCESS`, `env.MADEIRA_TLS_INDEX_SYNC`, `env.MADEIRA_UBI_CEF`, `env.MADEIRA_DESKTOP_CLOSE`.
  - `env.MADEIRA_DOCK_REGISTRY_REPAIR`, `env.MADEIRA_DOCK_REGISTRY_CREATE`, `env.MADEIRA_DOCK_STEAM_VIEWS`, `env.MADEIRA_DOCK_CEG_SERVICE_RESTART`.
  - `env.MADEIRA_DOCK_INSTALLERMESSAGE_PROVIDED`, `env.MADEIRA_PARADOX_LAUNCHER_MSI`, `env.MADEIRA_DIR_STORM`.
- 100 new host checks.

**Known issues:**
- External drives need BCD installed under its own identity: SideStore or AltStore, or a certificate signer with the bundle id changed to the certificate's App ID. Inside LiveContainer, or signed with a certificate that keeps BCD's original bundle id, iOS does not hand the chosen folder to BCD and **Open** in the folder picker does nothing. This is an iOS limit. Use exFAT or APFS; NTFS drives are read-only on iPhone and iPad.
- Red Dead Redemption 2 needs about 9.5 GB of RAM in play. Devices with 8 GB of RAM cannot hold it yet.
- GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2 from Steam: the Rockstar Launcher sometimes says Steam is not running (error 113, "please reinstall") although it is. Fully close BCD and start the game again. This build logs what the launcher sees, to find the cause.
- Very long GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2 sessions can stop when the emulator's memory area is full. Fully close BCD (swipe it away) and start again.
- Enshrouded and Hades II stop with a Steam "version mismatch": their Steam library is newer than the Steam client BCD Dock runs.
- The foldable iPhone's tabletop pose is in the code, but this build cannot read the hinge yet (it needs a newer iOS SDK).
- Windows Vulkan is new and tried on few games.

**Thanks** to @rbarton124, @pauloec, @iqui27, @creeper4004 and @Taala2 for their contributions to this release, and to Mila (mudcatpot) for the new icon.

Install help, game reports and ideas: join the [BCD-Games Discord](https://discord.gg/43TmupTVug).

**BCD.ipa**: the unsigned IPA, for sideloading with SideStore, AltStore or LiveContainer. It needs iOS 18 or later and JIT; the README has the details.
**BCD-source.tar.xz**: the complete source of this build with all its submodules (GPL-3.0).

versions.localizedDescription: What's New in v4.5.0 - Local Media Gallery: Scans downloaded media across Mori directories with categorized tabs (Video, Audio, Image, PDF), live counters, and persistent sorting (Newest, Oldest, A-Z, Size) - In-App Native PDF Viewer: Bundled offline PDF.js engine with high-DPI canvas rendering, viewport lazy rendering, page 1 cover generator, and page count subtitle - High-Resolution 640px Thumbnails: Upgraded Android native frame extraction, web canvas generator, and PDF covers to 640px JPEG with sequential queue processing - Audio Gallery Previews & Grid Covers: History-style audio playback in gallery viewer with album art, track details, local binary streaming, and album artwork on grid cards - Gallery Favorites Priority: Favorited items float to top of grid with heart badge, accent card border, and real-time cross-tab synchronization - In-App File Deletion: Cross-platform file deletion via trash button, card long-press haptic, or viewer modal with Android MediaScanner purge and Tauri backend support - Player Volume Toggle & Unmute Badge: Dedicated volume button in player bar, floating frosted-glass "Tap to unmute" badge for WebKit/macOS autoplay restrictions, and decoupled fullscreen toggle - Desktop Tauri Backend Commands: Implemented native Rust commands for recursive directory scanning (tauri_list_dir) and filesystem deletion (tauri_delete_file) - Instant Auto-Paste & Native Paste: Reduced clipboard check delay to 300ms on start/resume, with native paste event listener on input for instant link analysis - Privacy Lock Protection: Integrated Gallery with Mori PIN and biometric authentication with auto-lock on app pause/minimize - Gallery DOM Card Reuse: Map-based card caching preserves DOM nodes during filter and sort switches, eliminating decoder lag and image flicker - Scan Concurrency & Duplicate Fixes: Replaced boolean lock with active promise deduplication and resolved Android directory namespace prefixes to prevent duplicate media cards - Video Aspect Ratio & Local Loop Fixes: Enforced contain fit for 9:16 portrait videos in viewer and synchronized HTML loop attributes with ended fallback - Settings Audit & Cleanup: Purged orphaned auto-clear toggles in favor of day-based retention select menus, preventing accidental launch cache wipes

versions.localizedDescription: Since v1.1.0: the share-sheet import works from a cold start, and a pairing broadcast that never started is reported instead of hidden. ### What's fixed - **"Open in AirliftSilence" from the share sheet did nothing** (reported in #5). SwiftUI's `onOpenURL` never receives a document that another app opens while this app is cold-starting — the normal case for a sideloaded app that is not already running — so the request went nowhere. Document opens now arrive through `UIApplicationDelegate.application(_:open:options:)`, which does fire on a cold launch; `onOpenURL` keeps handling `airliftsilence://` URLs. Pairing files whose extension has no declared UTI (`.mobiledevicepairing`, `.mobilepairing`) are offered by the share sheet too, and a URL delivered twice is only imported once. - **A denied Local Network permission looked like a working app.** `NetService.publish()` fails silently without it, and Settings then never offers the **Pair with App** entry while the app kept saying "Advertising…". The status now reports what actually happened, error code included, and points at the permission. ### Install `AirliftSilence-v1.1.1.ipa` is **unsigned** — sign it with whatever you normally use (AltStore, SideStore, Sideloadly, TrollStore, …). Re-signing gives the app a fresh container, so export the pairing file first if you have a working one. Requires **iOS 18.0 – 27.2 beta 2**. Apple patched the underlying exploit in 27.2 beta 3. Also needs **LocalDevVPN** in loopback mode (never `127.0.0.1`), a **pairing record**, and the official **Apple Books** app opened at least once. ``` AirliftSilence-v1.1.1.ipa 3,348,064 bytes sha256 daa32fe3cbf4673178abbc9f297ceb1d25e463c2bb644eee5ad1679b7301ce4e ```

versions.localizedDescription: - **"Appears to be damaged" careers load.** A career saved on another device or install carries another player ID, and the game refused it as damaged although the file was fine. It now loads, and is saved with this device's ID from then on. - **Black Edition cars no longer invisible after loading a career.** The extra car records kept beside a save were only put back if the career matched them exactly, so one changed record left the cars invisible and without their upgrades. They now come back whenever the records that need them match. Thanks to [Lunquell](https://github.com/Lunquell) for reporting these ([issue 8](https://github.com/bep1s69/nfsmw-ios/issues/8)) and sending the save files and logs that found them. - **Smooth motion at 60 fps.** The game world and camera could judder, as if running at 30 fps, even though the fps counter showed a steady 60: worst in places you visit for the first time and right after restarting the device. The game timed each frame unevenly and moved the world by those uneven steps while the screen showed the frames evenly. Each frame now moves the world by exactly one screen refresh. - **Smoother 40 fps.** At the 40 fps cap the world moved in alternating short and long steps (the game's 60 Hz steps do not divide into 40), so it looked closer to 30 than the mirror and the map. The 40 cap now runs the game's simulation at 120 Hz: three even steps per frame. - **Battery mode lets you choose 30 or 40 fps** (it always forced 30). - **Custom HUD switch.** The HUD size and position settings now sit behind one Custom HUD switch, off by default: the game's own HUD unless you turn it on (your earlier changes come back when you do). - **No more stutter from the touch controls.** Steering or pressing the on-screen controls made a frame arrive one refresh late, so donuts and quick steering stuttered. The controls are now drawn as part of the game's picture. - **extra_args.txt saved as UTF-16 now works.** A file that went through the Mac (TextEdit, the clipboard) could be UTF-16, and every argument in it was ignored.

- **Import PC saves.** The save manager's Import also takes a save from the PC game (v1.3, the file inside the profile's folder, or a .zip of it): it is converted to the Xbox 360 layout. Needs one career of this game on the device already (its options are reused). - **Motion blur switch.** Motion blur can be turned off in the launcher and in the in-game options; off, the picture stays sharp when driving fast. - **Save sync between devices fixed.** Part of a Black Edition career was kept in a separate file the save manager ignored, so a newer save (for example one more challenge event) did not show as newer on the other device, and could arrive incomplete. That file now travels with the save everywhere, and saves are copied to your iCloud Drive folder shortly after the game saves, not only when the launcher opens. - **Delete saves from iCloud.** A save that is only in iCloud can now be deleted from the save manager (tap it), instead of only downloaded. - **Simpler save manager.** One list of careers. Each shows its cash, bounty and when and on which device it was last saved, including careers only in iCloud. When another device has a newer save, the career says so and tapping it offers "Use the save from iPad" first. Sync now is the button at the top right. - **Import saves from the internet.** The save manager's Import button takes an Xbox 360 save file, a Xenia save folder or .zip, a .zip exported from the app, or the bare save file. - **Achievements follow you between devices.** With an iCloud Drive folder chosen, an achievement unlocked on one device now shows as unlocked on the others too. - **Black Edition content now actually turns on.** The switch set the wrong byte of the game's memory, so the content stayed hidden. Now the 70th Challenge Series event (the Camaro) and the Black Edition cars in Quick Race appear, and starting a career works. It is always on now: the launcher no longer has a switch for it. - **Smoother frame pacing with the FPS counter on.** Each counter update delayed a frame, a small stutter up to twice a second; the counter is now drawn into the game's picture (a square dark box). At the 60 fps cap frames are also made in step with the screen's refresh, as at 30 and 40. - **120 Hz simulation switch.** The game can move its world 120 times a second instead of 60 (Advanced tab, off by default; always on with the 120 fps cap). - **Options while playing.** In a menu or the pause screen, tap the gear at the top right (or press L3+R3 on a controller) to change the render resolution, MetalFX, the 30/60 fps cap, anti-aliasing and the battery settings without restarting. Settings that need a restart (40/120 fps, MSAA) are marked "next launch". - **HUD size and position.** New HUD settings (launcher Graphics tab and the options while playing): the race HUD's size and safe zone (how close to the screen's edges it sits), and the minimap, the speedometer and the race info (standings, laps, times) moved left, right, up or down on their own. - **Post-processing switch fixed.** Turning it off now really removes the colour filter, bloom and vignette; it can also be changed while playing. - **Battery mode now caps the game at 30 fps**, along with its other savings. - **New setting: reflection and mirror resolution.** The reflections on the cars and the rear-view mirror are drawn at the Xbox 360's size (the default, lighter) or follow the render resolution (a sharper mirror). - **About a quarter less battery drain while playing**, with the same picture, resolution and frame rate: the game's threads ask iOS for a lower priority, so the CPU runs at cheaper speeds (measured on an iPad Pro M4 at 1.5x / 60 fps). On by default on devices with at least 6 efficiency cores (M-series iPads); off on iPhones, where it made the game stutter. Open the app. 2. Complete the login flow in the web view that shows up (passkeys don’t work here, so make sure you have another form of 2FA if applicable). 3. The app may crash, that’s normal (it helps ensure the credentials are saved). 4. Reopen the app, and you should be at your “For you” page! ## New Features ### From v6 * Added a feature to hide Blue checkmark tweets from the timeline and standalone replies in comment sections. contributors section to the NeoFreeBird settings page. * Added option to directly copy user URL. * Added option to hide the “typing” indicator in Chat. * Added a toggle to show unrounded counts, as well as added the ability to show the unrounded number of tweets. * The News tab is now hidden. * Added an option to disable the gesture to dock videos. * Added option to download voice messages (due to how XChat encrypts attachments, you need to play the message to have the option to download it). * Added ability to upload in 1080p (and 4k, but this is technically unsupported). * Added option to see poll results before voting. * Added option to tap to play/pause video with 2 fingers. * Added option to see where an account is located in a tweet. * Added option to disable screenshot detection in XChat (broken as of now, although I have a private fix) * Added option to disable the new media carousel (switches back to old grid view). * Added ability to remove retweets of tweets from users who’ve blocked you (please fix this X). * Doomscrolling can now be turned off with disabling video scroll. * Added ability to use Tenor GIFs instead of GIPHY. * Added option to export and import settings (no more coming soon!). * Added option to always download the highest-quality MP4 file from media downloads. * Added option to stop X from losing focus when staying out of the app for a long time. * Added option to hide Message button on tweets. * Added a “Download all Videos” button (only works when all media items are videos). * Added option to see quote and retweet numbers (with an option for unrounded counts). * Added an option to play a custom sound (under 7 seconds and with the AAC format) when a tweet is posted. * Hide the “Download Grok Bot” button on Grok Tweets. * # LiveContainer 3.8.0 > [!Warning] > The standalone version requires **SideStore 0.6.2+** or **AltStore 2.2.1+** for installation. > To install LiveContainer with built-in SideStore (`LiveContainer+SideStore.ipa`), please use [Impactor](https://github.com/khcrysalis/Impactor) or [iloader](https://github.com/nab138/iloader). See [our installation guide](https://livecontainer.github.io/docs/installation/lc_sidestore) for details. # New Features ## Storage Management - Added a new storage management view with a breakdown of app bundles, containers, temporary files, app group data, tweaks, and other files. (Hidden apps' size is included in "other" section until unlocked) - Added per-app storage details, including app bundle size, container sizes, and last-used date. - Added actions to clean temporary files and caches, including guest app caches and LiveContainer's own caches. ## Multiple LiveContainers - Added configurable launch priority for multiple LiveContainer instances, making shared-app shortcuts choose available instances in the order you prefer. (#1367) ## Share to Apps in LiveContainer Added a share extension to LiveContainer. When you share a URL or a file from iOS's share sheet, LiveContainer will ask which app you would like to open the URL/file in, so the old share to LiveContainer shortcut method is no longer needed. When an ipa file is shared in this way, LiveContainer will ask if you want to install it in LiveContainer or in the built-in SideStore (if installed) (#1357) ## Multitasking - Added per-app multitask preferences. Each app can now follow the global setting, always launch in multitask mode, or avoid multitask mode. (#1208) - Improved multitask dock behavior: the dock can be made smaller, hidden more cleanly, and has improved padding. (#1228, #1250) - Added more multitask window animations and improved native-window scene handling. - URL schemes and `open-url` payloads can be passed to already-running multitask apps and native windows. ## JIT - Added StosDebug support as a JIT enabler. ## TweakLoader You can now disable tweaks in the "Tweaks" page in LiveContainer's UI. by @SAOMDVN # Improvements - Added support for manually setting a container's IDFV. (#1194) - IDFV spoofing works even when Tweakloader is not loaded. - Reworked signing logic for tweaks and app installation, with multithreaded signing support. - Download alerts now block tab switching while a download is in progress. - Crash reports are shown in a sheet instead of a large alert for better performance on newer iOS versions. - Add a "Clear Notification" button (#1388) - Added some popular NSBonjourServices keys so apps can discover AirPlay devices and remote pairing pairable hosts in the local network. (#1417) # Bug Fixes - Fixed `livecontainer://open-url` dropping the deep link when launching an app from a cold start. (#1339) - Fixed the Add to Home Screen menu failing or behaving incorrectly by replacing the SwiftUI context menu implementation. (#1209) - Fixed a crash when opening Container Preferences if the app did not contain an `en.lproj` path. (#1239) - Fixed apps and AltStore sources not being searchable in some cases. (#1365, #1368) - Fixed converting a shared app back to private after aborting an install with the same bundle identifier, which could leave stale container state behind. (#1347) - Fixed shortcuts and JIT flows getting stuck on a busy LiveContainer instance instead of using another available instance. (#1386) - Fixed file picker not workings for some apps because Tweakloader is not loaded after enabling "Hide LiveContainer from dyld API". (#1430) - Fixed several app launch compatibility issues on iOS 26.5 beta, and some multitask/JIT app launches. (#1300, #1310, #1329) - Fixed multitask keyboard focus issues on iOS 17.4+, including cases where the keyboard would not appear, Passwords would immediately close, or video playback would freeze in multitask mode. (#1402, #844, #870) - Added support for iOS 27 developer beta.

# LiveContainer 3.7.0 > [!Warning] > The standalone version requires **SideStore 0.6.2+** or **AltStore 2.2.1+** for installation. > We recommend installing LiveContainer + SideStore using [Impactor](https://github.com/khcrysalis/Impactor) or [iloader](https://github.com/nab138/iloader). See [our installation guide](https://livecontainer.github.io/docs/installation/lc_sidestore) for details. Happy Spring Festival / Lunar New Year! After six months of development, we’re excited to release **LiveContainer 3.7.0**. This update introduces several powerful new features, including the Launch App Shortcut, iOS 26 JIT script support, external containers, native icon generation, and more. # New Features ## Launch App Shortcut > [!Note] > This feature requires LiveContainer to be installed with at least the **LaunchAppExtension** and **LaunchAppExtensionHelper** extension. iOS 16+ is supported. A new extension allows apps to launch instantly without opening the LiveContainer main interface (for apps that are not locked, hidden, or JIT-required). Once configured, the shortcut prepares the runtime environment and selects an available LiveContainer instance to launch the app directly. This reduces extra relaunches and jumps and typically saves 1~2 seconds per launch. See the [setup guide](https://livecontainer.github.io/docs/guides/add-to-home-screen) for instructions. ## JIT Support for iOS 26 JIT scripts has been added by @Vishram1123. Scripts can be configured in app-specific settings and loaded automatically on iOS 26+. The **“StikDebug in another LiveContainer”** option has been fixed, allowing StikDebug to run within LiveContainer. When launching a JIT-required app, LiveContainer will automatically detect StikDebug, launch it in an available container, and pass all required parameters — including scripts — to enable JIT. In addition, when enabling JIT for multitasked app, LiveContainer will prioritize launching StikDebug as a multitask app to save app slot usage. (TODO: this doesn’t automatically minimize StikDebug after enabling JIT, might be added later) Be sure to convert StikDebug into a shared app before use. ## External Containers > [!Note] > Containers stored on external media (portable drives, SMB shares, etc.) are unsupported by many apps and may cause instability or crashes. You can now use external folders as app containers. This is useful if you want to manage app data through a file manager while still accessing it in LiveContainer, or if you want maintain container access when an app is shared. To configure this, open: **App-Specific Settings → Select External Data Folder** ## Native Icons LiveContainer now generates icons using native iOS libraries. On iOS 18+, this enables proper Light, Dark, and Original (Liquid Glass) icon rendering. These icons can also be saved for home screen shortcuts. ## Multitasking Improvements * Added **“Skip app terminate screen”** (by @boa-z) * Added **”Single Window Mode”** to minimize other apps when a maximized app is brought to front * Launch URL schemes can now be passed to multitasking apps. Passing URL between multitask apps can be controlled via **”Redirect URL to Host”** switch * Launching Private Apps is now possible. By default, apps launched with private container is only given sandbox access to its own data container folder. You can change it in developer settings. * Changed animations a little bit ## AltStore Source Support Basic AltSource support has been implemented by @StephenDev0. Sources can be added using: ``` livecontainer://sources?url=<URL> ``` ## Other Additions * App remarks are now supported (by @WingCH) * Decrypted apps can now be installed via `itms-services` links (by @WingCH) # Bug Fixes * Fixed iOS 26.4b1 compatibility (#1152) * Fixed crashes caused by `-[NSUserDefaults synchronize]` returning NO * Fixed signing crashes when apps contain too many libraries (#1135) * Fixed signing failure when not enough space is available to insert HM_DYLIB in Mach-O headers

This option is available in the LiveContainer settings. 7. The window hosting PiP is now automatically hidden, and is restored when dismissing PiP. ## App Management 1. You can now double-tap an app to quickly open its settings. By @m1337v. 2. Apps can now be sorted by name (A–Z, Z–A), last opened date, installation date, or a custom order, allowing you to arrange them however you like. By @boa-z and @m1337v. 3. You can now view an app's installation date and last launch date in its settings. ## [EXPERIMENTAL] Built-in SideStore This experimental feature combines both LiveContainer and SideStore into a single app, saving one app slot for other standalone apps. You can try it out by downloading "LiveContainer+SideStore.ipa". Currently, SideStore itself, the refresh shortcut, and the widget are functional. See here for all changes made to original SideStore https://github.com/hugeBlack/SideStore/tree/LiveContainerSupport > [!Note] > LiveProcess is required to use the refresh shortcut. > It has been reported that the built-in SideStore cannot determine the device UDID if the standalone SideStore is running in the background. If you encounter this issue, please terminate the standalone SideStore. > [!Warning] > Logging into built-in SideStore will save your credentials to LiveContainer's keychain access group. Even though LiveContainer implements isolated keychain access, it is not guaranteed to be completely bulletproof. As such, malicious apps may be able to extract credentials from built-in SideStore. Please consider migrating to a burner Apple ID if you tend to install apps from unknown sources. # Improvements ## App Switching Between LiveContainer/LiveContainer2/LiveProcess We’ve implemented a new method to directly check whether LiveContainer or LiveContainer2 is running, enabling more accurate detection of running apps. In this version, LiveContainer will automatically switch to a running app or launch an app using an idle LiveContainer. ## UserDefaults/Preferences We've adopted a new UserDefaults/Preferences hook that is more efficient and capable of redirecting more preference reads/writes to the app’s container. ## Language Switching We’ve introduced a new language switching mechanism that now also applies to LiveProcess without affecting LiveContainer’s own language settings. # Bug Fixes 1. Fixed an issue where some apps displayed a black screen in versions 3.5.0/3.5.1. Fixes #543, #594. 2. Fixed an issue where some apps bypassed `SecItem*` hooks using `dlsym`. Fix #339. 3. Fixed issues with signing and patching apps wh

# ⚠️This version ⚠️REQUIRES⚠️ SideStore 0.6.0+ / AltStore 2.0+ to install. >[!NOTE] > This a minor release that solves the following issues in version 3.5.0. For more information, please see [3.5.0 release note](https://github.com/LiveContainer/LiveContainer/releases/tag/3.5.0). # Improvement Fix #590: We adopted a new method for relaunching LiveContainer which makes apps launch faster compared to 3.5.0. by @khanhduytran0 # Bug Fix Fix Liquid Glass option need to be toggled off and on in order to work. It's off by default now and you can toggle it on in iOS Settings -> Apps -> LiveContainer -> Enable Liquid Glass

# ⚠️This version ⚠️REQUIRES⚠️ SideStore 0.6.0+ / AltStore 2.0+ to install. >[!Note] > We recommend using SideStore 0.6.2-20250420.25+ or AltStore 2.2.1+ to import your certificate directly, without needing to apply a patch when setting up JIT-Less mode. After two months of development, we're proud to announce the release of LiveContainer 3.5.0! This update brings powerful new features like multitasking and better ADP certificate support, along with several bug fixes, improvements, and new language translations. # Multitasking One of LiveContainer’s main limitations has been the inability to open more than one app at a time. Our new multitasking feature addresses that. You can now launch multiple apps simultaneously in in-app virtual windows. These windows can be resized, scaled, and even displayed using the native Picture-in-Picture (PiP) feature. On iPads, apps can run in native window mode, displaying each app in a separate system window. And if you wish, you can choose to run apps in multitasking mode by default in settings. To use multitasking: 1. Convert the app you want to multitask into a **shared app**. 2. Hold its banner and tap **"Multitask"**. >[!Note] >1. To use multitasking, ensure you select **"Keep Extension"** when installing via SideStore/AltStore. >2. Most common apps are compatible, but some may have issues. >3. If you want to enable JIT for multitasked apps, you’ll need a JIT enabler that supports attaching by PID — coming soon in StikDebug. # ADP Certificate Support LiveContainer now officially supports ADP development certificates. Thanks to PR #537 by @SoY0ung, LiveContainer uses the app group included in your `.mobileprovision` file, rather than hard-coded SideStore/AltStore app groups. This unlocks multitasking and other features. >[!Note] >1. Only **development certificates** are supported. >2. To use multitasking, your `.mobileprovision` must contain at least one app group. >3. To enable keychain separation, LiveContainer must be signed with all 128 required keychain access groups. >4. We recommend changing LiveContainer's bundle ID to match the `application-identifier` in your `.mobileprovision`. # iOS 26 Liquid Glass Support Although LiveContainer is currently built with iOS 18.2 SDK, we include an option to enable Liquid Glass for LiveContainer's UI if you have upgraded to iOS 26. You can find this option in iOS Settings-> Apps -> LiveContainer -> enable Liquid Glass. # Improvements - Optimized app launching process for faster startup: - No longer moves shared app data to a private folder. - Uses a new method to override the main executable path, avoiding SIGSEGV signal handlers. - Removed app lock and use container lock only. - Added `.tipa` support (#467). Note: this allows installing `.tipa` files, but does not mean the app will run properly without correct entitlements. - You can now search for apps in the app list. - Renamed StikJIT (Standalone) to StikDebug. # Bug Fixes - Fixed #200 by directly setting `dyld.config.process.mainExecutablePath` to app's real main executable path, ensuring `_NSGetExecutablePath` returns the correct value. - Fixed #326 by correcting an error in `Info.plist`. Note: HealthKit entitlements are still required to access health data. - Alleviate #423 by avoiding dyld library validation bypass on signed apps, which otherwise prevents apps that requires JIT from executing JIT pages on A15+ - Fixed #478 by moving the JIT enabling window to `LCAppListView`. - Fixed #476 by updating ZSign. - Fixed #497 by resolving an issue in dyld library validation bypass. - Fixed iOS 16.2 (#495) and iOS 18.4+ on iPad 7 (#531). - Fixed #518 by sending KVO notifications when UsedDefaults is changed. - Fixed #582 by invalidating duplicate library load commands. # Deprecated Features ## SideStore/AltStore Patching With SideStore 0.6.2-20250420.25 and AltStore 2.2.1 both supporting certificate export, patching these stores is no longer necessary. This feature is now deprecated and will be re

# ⚠️This version ⚠️REQUIRES⚠️ SideStore 0.6.0+ / AltStore 2.0+ to install. This version improved app re-signing experience, add support for new JIT enablers, increased compatibility with relatively old apps and add translation for Arabic, French, German, Japanese, Portuguese and Swedish. >[!Note] LiveContainer has upgraded SDK version to 18.2, which breaks some apps that works on previous versions. Fortunately we have developed the "Spoof SDK Version" feature, forcing system libraries to operate in the SDK version the app is built with. You can enable "Spoof SDK Version". # New Features ## 1. New Re-Sign Strategy Instead of keeping track of expiration date, LiveContainer now directly ask iOS to determine whether the code signature is valid, which significantly decreases app re-sign rate. For now your apps will be re-signed only if their code signature is invalid, which probably happens when your certificate is expired (usually takes a year), or is revoked (when you reinstall SideStore/AltStore). ## 2. Support for StikJIT(StikDebug), SideStore JIT [StikJIT(StikDebug)](https://github.com/StephenDev0/StikJIT) is the newest on-device JIT enabler powered by [idevice](https://github.com/jkcoxson/idevice). You can now install it both as a standalone app or install it inside LiveContainer. See #265 item 5.8 for more information. SideStore has recently switched its backend to idevice and added on-device JIT support. For now its JIT URL Scheme has not been implemented so you have to manually enable JIT for LiveContainer. ## 3. Spoof SDK version Spoofing SDK version forces system libraries to operate in the SDK version the app is built with. This fix works surprisingly well so we decided to enable it by default for newly installed apps. This fixes some old apps crashing because of the new SDK. We also removed the "Bypass AssertBarrierOnQueue" fix since the root cause is SDK version. Fix #421 #422 ## 4. Support Import Certificate From SideStore With [this SideStore pr](https://github.com/SideStore/SideStore/pull/959), we can now directly retrieve certificate from SideStore (0.6.2-20250420.25+) without the patch, thus simplifying the process of enabling JIT-Less mode. ## 5. Game Mode Support With the SDK version upgrade, LiveContainer now supports game mode. If you don't need it, you can turn it off in the control center. # Bug Fixes 1. Fix a regression caused by NSBundle path fix. Fix #409 2. Keep app's plugin folder in case some apps need files inside. Fix hugeBlack/LiveContainer#43 3. Add TPRO rw in overwrite exec path in case the executable path is TPRO protected. Fix #327 4. Replace all `withCheckedContinuation` with `withUnsafeContinuation` to solve crash on iOS 18.0 beta. Fix #435 5. Add file permission to solve some sign issues. Fix #448 # Removed Features The following features are removed because it's not useful in current version or constantly causing issues. 1. AltSign: We drop AltSign support because it's constantly causing issues and it's relatively old. 2. Bypass AssertBarrierOnQueue: It is replaced by "Spoof SDK version" 3. Sign Only on Signature Expires: It's now useless as we directly determine if an app's code signature is valid by asking the system. # Translation LiveContainer is now translated into Arabic, Simplified Chinese, French, German, Japanese, Portuguese and Swedish - Arabic: translated by dlshad2 - French: translated by @p-sage - German: translated by @BeityBytes - Japanese: translated by @naolad - Portuguese: translated by damn_the_daniel - Swedish: translated by @se2crid # Credit Shout out to @khanhduytran0 for doing a lot of research under the hood! # Other LiveContainer is now migrated from a Theos project to a Xcode project, which simplifies the development and significantly decreased Github Actions build time (2 minutes now and around 10 minutes previously)

versions.localizedDescription: ## 主要变化 本版改进异常会话恢复和停止处理，并新增可选的后台定位指示器设置。 - **异常中断后可恢复**：坐标写入失败或停止未获设备确认时，保留上次位置与路线进度，无需重启 App 即可选择继续模拟或恢复真实位置。 - **停止等待有了限时**：坐标写入和位置清除增加超时处理，避免设备无响应时一直停留在“正在停止”。未确认清除成功时，仍会保留恢复入口。 - **改善后台保持处理**：定位服务遇到暂时错误时保留更新请求；返回前台后重新检查权限和后台保持状态，首页提示后台保持不可用的情况。 - **新增“减少后台定位指示器”**：默认关闭，主动开启后需要“始终”定位权限。未获得该权限时保持原有显示行为；关闭开关不会撤回已授予的权限，可在系统设置中修改。 - **补充隧道跳转说明**：列表用于选择自动打开的应用，不限制兼容软件。其他代理或 VPN 软件只要正确配置兼容设备隧道，也可手动开启后使用。 ## 下载与安装 - 标准版：`WrapPin-Standard-1.0.18-build61-unsigned.ipa`，供 SideStore 或其他自签方式使用。 - 隧道版：`WrapPin-Tunnel-1.0.18-build61-unsigned.ipa`，需要带 Packet Tunnel 权限的签名证书及描述文件。 - 两个版本均为未签名 IPA，最低系统为 iOS 27.0。免费 Apple 账号和 SideStore 请使用标准版。 SHA-256： - 标准版：`a897774a0dee14f8c2c7a24a9c97eaa041d281c441f116d1613f5164d92aaa57` - 隧道版：`62e66c1036d1046532e30ed1d3e604f06403d8f01afa85988ad40e1d5d037ff2` ## 验证与边界 - 维护者已用 Build 60 在真机上验证主要功能，未逐项记录测试清单。Build 61 的功能代码相同，本身尚未独立装机。 - 两个 scheme 的 Debug、Release 构建，8 个检查脚本及 Rust 10 项单元测试均通过。 - 这次提供异常中断后的手动恢复，不会自动重连，也不保证所有后台连接都能持续。 - 坐标写入和清除分别有 15 秒限时；写入接近限时才完成、随后清除又超时时，停止可能接近 30 秒。限时以 App 能够正常执行为前提。 - 指示器的最终显示由 iOS 决定，系统可能定期提醒后台定位使用。后台保持收到的坐标仍不保存、不上传。 - 从多任务界面划掉 App 会结束模拟连接；VPN 仍显示已连接，不代表模拟仍在生效。 - 原有蜂窝网络限制不变：通过 Shadowrocket、Surge、Loon 建立设备连接仍不可靠，建议使用 Wi-Fi。

apps.localizedDescription: OldOS is a testament to the days of yesteryear, showcasing what iOS once was ten years ago. The ethos of the app is to merge the technologies of today with a pixel-perfect recreation of the user experience of the past. The vast majority of apps in OldOS are fully functional — meaning they seamlessly integrate with the data on your phone to deliver a live, emulator-esque experience. What does this mean? Well, you can play your music in iPod, get directions in Maps, surf the web in Safari, view the current weather in Weather, and much more. By the same token, no shortcuts were taken in fully fleshing out the operating system. You can change your background, adjust settings, search apps, et cetera. There are a few apps still not ready for primetime but don't worry, they're coming soon. With OldOS, you no longer need to worry about securing a legacy iPhone to experience nostalgia — it's available on your daily driver. Part of the goal with OldOS is to enable anyone to understand how iOS works and demonstrate just how powerful SwiftUI truly is. For that reason, the entire app is open-sourced — enabling developers to learn about, modify, and add to the app. I thought building this over my last six or so months in high school and sharing it with the world would be a fun and productive endeavor.

In doing so, the codebase has been retooled and refactored, APIs have been restored, and compilation errors have been resolved. versions.localizedDescription: Built on scrcpy **v4.0** (SDL3 + FFmpeg 8.1.1). ### Fixes **Mirrored picture geometry** - Fix the picture overflowing the window and not being draggable back. The porting layer applied `SDL_SetRenderScale(nativeScale)` on top of the density conversion scrcpy v4 already performs, magnifying the geometry by density × nativeScale (4× on @2x, 9× on @3x). - Fix the picture being offset to one side from the moment a session connects. The Stage Manager resize path compared the view size in pixels against `SDL_GetWindowSize()`, which SDL3 reports in points, so the sizes never matched and every layout pass pushed a resize event carrying a pixel-sized geometry. **Black screen on high-contrast scene changes** - A full display-layer queue is normal back-pressure; it no longer escalates to flushing the queue and restarting the server-side encoder after 5 dropped frames. Recovery now requires a sustained stall, and the reset cooldown was raised so a second reset cannot land before the previous restart has produced a keyframe. **Disk filling with logs** - The active log file is now bounded at runtime (previously only older files were cleaned, and only at cold start — one user reported a single 76 GB log). - Decoder and render error logs are rate-limited; they previously wrote one line per packet or per frame for as long as the error persisted. **Crashes and background behaviour** - Fix `SIGTRAP`/`SIGABRT` during teardown (`sc_server_destroy`, `sc_main_thread_destroy`, `sc_screen_destroy`/`sc_fps_counter_destroy`) when a session is re-entered in the same process. - Fix the background timeout ignoring the configured duration, and a background-task handle leak that could disconnect an already-disconnected session. - Fix a VNC connect crash and a blank screen after ADB disconnect. ### Install The attached IPA is **Ad Hoc signed** and installs only on devices registered to the developer account. For general use, install via TestFlight or the App Store.

versions.localizedDescription: # ByeTunes v2.6 – Favorites, Playlist Pinning & Background Downloads Reworked Hi guys, here is the 2.6 update for ByeTunes. A good amount of things got added, fixed and improved in this one. You can now properly favorite injected songs, pin playlists from inside ByeTunes, and keep downloads going in the background with a new Picture in Picture window. There were also a bunch of fixes around metadata, library management and database safety. **Favorites** There are three new options inside Library Repair: - **Create Favorites Playlist** creates the Favorites playlist using the right name for your device region. - **Fix Missing Favorites** repairs songs injected with an older version that you already favorited but that never actually appeared in Favorites. - **Delete Favorites Playlist** lets you delete that playlist from Library Repair. Songs injected from 2.6 onwards now get their store IDs during injection, so you can favorite them right away. If the metadata fetcher finds a match, ByeTunes uses the IDs from that match. Songs without a match get generated IDs instead. **Quick recommendation:** if you have older injected songs that you favorited but cannot find in Favorites, run **Fix Missing Favorites** inside Library Repair. **Playlist Pinning** You can now pin and unpin playlists from the On-Device Library. Long-press a playlist or use the Pin button from inside it. **Keep in mind: pinning and unpinning these playlists needs to be done through ByeTunes. The Pin option inside the Apple Music app does not work for them.** **Background Downloads** Background downloads got a big rework. ByeTunes now uses silent audio to keep downloads going in the background, with an optional Picture in Picture window so you can see what is happening after leaving the app. The window shows the current song's progress, what is next in the queue, and when metadata is being fetched. You can also customize it with themes, your own colors or a background picture. There is a live preview in Settings so you can see how it looks before using it. This replaces the old background download behavior and Live Activity support. Download progress now shows in the Picture in Picture window. If the app closes while songs are still downloading, those songs go back to the front of the queue the next time you open ByeTunes. Pause and Cancel were fixed too. They now properly stop background transfers instead of accidentally starting a fallback download after you already paused or cancelled the song. **Download Queue & Saving Files** Downloaded songs now get their metadata as part of the download process. You will see a "fetching metadata" state before the song is marked as done, instead of that work being left to a separate background metadata manager. A few other things got added or improved: - **Clear All** for completed items in the queue sheet. - Preview buttons in the album sheet and artist profile. - Icons instead of text in the download queue indicator. - Downloads are now limited to **2 at a time for MP3 and 1 for FLAC**, matching what the server supports. (This is temporal until I can pay for a better provider) - A **server status banner** appears when the server goes into maintenance. Downloads are blocked while the server is down. - A new **Save With Fetched Metadata** toggle that writes the fetched tags and cover artwork into the MP3 and FLAC copies you save. **Metadata Fixes** Metadata matching got a lot of attention in this update. There were cases where a remix could get the original song's information, or a song could get renamed to a different track from the same album. Those issues should now be fixed. - Downloaded songs now look up the exact Deezer track and album. An Apple Music match is only accepted if it belongs to the same album. - Apple Music track matching now checks the title, so songs should no longer get relabeled as another track from that album. - Apple Music search pages are requested in English so ByeTunes can find the Songs and Albu

versions.localizedDescription: BlueWake 0.9.0 makes the Mac, iPhone and iPad builds as fast as the PC builds, fixes the camera dipping with the right-stick camera, stops the flicker with Smooth Motion, and brings one settings menu to every computer. Every version needs your own USA (GZLE01) disc image. The ready-made Windows build includes the game code translated from my disc; nothing else from the game is included. ### Install **Windows:** download `BlueWake-v0.9.0-windows-x64.zip`, unpack the whole folder and run `BlueWake.exe`. Your saves and settings in `%APPDATA%\BlueWake` carry over. You need Windows 10 or 11 and a CPU with AVX2. SHA-256 of the zip: `3c0edc36241fc1783693e1a9fa942995f4f32efec14fb3a9afc889a595da61ce`. BlueWake.exe isn't code-signed, so a new build can be flagged by mistake; check the SHA-256 and see [If Windows says it's a virus](https://github.com/chrissotraidis/bluewake/blob/main/docs/WINDOWS.md#if-windows-says-its-a-virus). **iPhone and iPad:** build your app with [PadMint](https://github.com/chrissotraidis/padmint/releases/latest) on an Apple Silicon Mac. It downloads `BlueWake-v0.9.0-ios-unsigned.ipa` (the app without game code) and adds the game made from your disc, now with the faster preparations below. Install it over your current BlueWake to keep your saves. **Mac:** build it from this release's source: `scripts/builder/build.sh "/path/to/GZLE01.iso" --platform macos --out build/macos`. Your saves in `~/Library/Application Support/BlueWake` are kept. **Linux:** build it from this release's source with `python3 scripts/linux/build.py /path/to/GZLE01.iso` (steps in `docs/LINUX.md`). The container build works again at the player's CPU target. Contributors have built the AppImage from this release's commit with their own discs; a ready-made one will be added to this release once it's checked and uploaded. **Android (experimental):** build it yourself from your own disc, as `docs/ANDROID.md` describes; the builder now runs on a Mac as well as Windows. ### What's new **Much faster on Mac, iPhone and iPad** - Builds you make with PadMint or the builder now get the same module preparations and behaviour timing as the Windows and Linux builds. On the benchmark tour that's 75 to 79% more game frames a second on an iPad Pro (M2) and 64 to 77% on an M3 Max, with a smaller game module and a much shorter build. At normal speed the iPad's game thread is about half idle. `--conservative` builds it the old way. **Fixes** - The camera no longer dips for a frame every few seconds with **Direct right-stick camera and aiming** on (thanks to jslay88). - No more flicker with Smooth Motion above 60 FPS in the HD look, the clouds, the wave crests and swimming (thanks to pdale-boop). - Linux builds at the player's CPU target again (thanks to jslay88). **One menu on every computer** (thanks to pdale-boop) - Windows, Mac and Linux draw the same settings menu from one list, with controller navigation, contrast and text size, a Config tab, greyed settings that say why, and pausing under the menu as a setting. **Controls** - A controller can keep playing while another window is in front (Controls, off by default). - Keep the right-stick camera but aim with the left stick: turn off **The right stick aims too (first person, items)**. - On iPhone and iPad, the menu's switches keep the menu open, so you can change several settings in one visit. **HD textures from a real Wind Waker HD disc image** (thanks to jkoehler11) - The importer reads the content a real WUD/WUX stores, takes a key file, a pasted key or an emulator `keys.txt` as it is, keeps the form after a mistake, and says what it imported and skipped. **Also new** - Sun shadows from a shadow map in the HD look, so what's off screen still casts a shadow (thanks to pdale-boop). Off by default, under Mods › Experimental. - A sea compass switch: the red end points the way you're sailing (thanks to jslay88). Off by default, with Better Wind Waker's settings. - On iPhone, iPad and Android, **Share Session Lo

BlueWake 0.8.0 brings the Wind Waker HD look, HD textures you make from your own Wind Waker HD game inside the app, more speed by default on Windows and Linux, the same menus on every computer, and an experimental Android build. Every version needs your own USA (GZLE01) disc image. The ready-made Windows build includes the game code translated from my disc; nothing else from the game is included. ### Install **Windows:** download `BlueWake-v0.8.0-windows-x64.zip`, unpack the whole folder and run `BlueWake.exe`. Your saves and settings in `%APPDATA%\BlueWake` carry over. You need Windows 10 or 11 and a CPU with AVX2. A Direct3D 12 GPU is best. On older GPUs BlueWake now tries Direct3D 11 instead of showing a black screen; I haven't been able to check that on such a PC yet, so tell me how it goes. **Linux:** build it from this release's source with `python3 scripts/linux/build.py /path/to/GZLE01.iso` (steps in `docs/LINUX.md`). A ready-made AppImage will be added to this release once one is built and checked. **iPhone and iPad:** build your app with [PadMint](https://github.com/chrissotraidis/padmint/releases/latest) on an Apple Silicon Mac. It downloads `BlueWake-v0.8.0-ios-unsigned.ipa` (the app without game code) and adds the game made from your disc. Install it over your current BlueWake to keep your saves. **Mac:** build it from this release's source: `scripts/builder/build.sh "/path/to/GZLE01.iso" --platform macos --out build/macos`. Your saves in `~/Library/Application Support/BlueWake` are kept. **Android (experimental):** build it yourself from your own disc on a Windows PC, as `docs/ANDROID.md` describes (thanks to LiquidAzir). It's checked on one phone so far. ### What's new **The Wind Waker HD look**, off by default - Islands on the horizon from further away, bloom, the far-distance blur, ambient occlusion, cloud shadows, and edge and torch light, kept gentle so the game keeps its colours. Press **F2** on Windows, Mac and Linux, or turn it on under **Mods** on iPhone and iPad. Each piece can be turned off by itself (`docs/WWHD_LOOK.md`). **HD textures from your own Wind Waker HD game** - **Mods › Wind Waker HD textures › Import from Wind Waker HD…** makes the texture pack, HD menus and HUD included, from your decrypted HD dump or a USA WUD/WUX image with its keys, on Windows, Mac, Linux, iPhone and iPad. No Python, and nothing from the Wii U game is included in BlueWake. **Faster** - Behaviour timing is on by default on Windows and Linux: 7 to 11% faster on Intel desktops and 9% on the Steam Deck. - Lighter checks around the game code (thanks to pdale-boop) and Elliott Tate's faster returns and calls. - On Wayland the game runs at full speed (thanks to jslay88). **The same menus and keys on every computer** (thanks to pdale-boop) - F1 settings, F2 the HD look, F5 and F8 save and load state, F7 the stage select, F9 the frame rate, F10 Smooth Motion, F11 fullscreen. The Windows menu works with a controller, and Linux gets Restart now and safe mode. **Controls** - The D-pad moves the cursor in Items and Quest Status, gyro aiming with a DualSense, DualShock 4, Switch Pro or Steam Deck, swapping L and R, and 21:9 widescreen. **Fixes** - Lenzo accepts the right Picto Box photos (thanks to jslay88). - Each island's sea chart shows its own map. - The Greatfish merchant stays on his raft (thanks to jslay88). - Resizing the window on Linux no longer crashes (thanks to pdale-boop). **Also new** - The developers' stage select, off by default, with 468 places to jump to from your own file (thanks to pdale-boop). - Linux: portable mode, a working texture-pack folder picker (thanks to jkoehler11), and the build container (thanks to cforain). ### How it was checked I built the Windows version on my PC (Ryzen 7 5700U) from my own disc, from the same commit, in 81 minutes. It starts, draws with Direct3D 12 and quits cleanly; I only tried it briefly at Outset this time. I built the iPhone and iPad app without game code from this releas

BlueWake 0.7.0 is faster, especially on older and smaller CPUs, and fixes several controller problems. Every version needs your own USA (GZLE01) disc image. The ready-made Windows build includes the game code translated from my disc; nothing else from the game is included. ### Install **Windows:** download `BlueWake-v0.7.0-windows-x64.zip`, unpack the whole folder and run `BlueWake.exe`. Your saves and settings in `%APPDATA%\BlueWake` carry over. You need Windows 10 or 11, a Direct3D 12 GPU, and a CPU with AVX2. **iPhone and iPad:** build your app with [PadMint](https://github.com/chrissotraidis/padmint/releases/latest) on an Apple Silicon Mac. It downloads `BlueWake-v0.7.0-ios-unsigned.ipa` (the app without game code) and adds the game made from your disc. Install it over your current BlueWake to keep your saves. **Linux:** build it from this release's source with `python3 scripts/linux/build.py /path/to/GZLE01.iso` (steps in `docs/LINUX.md`). A ready-made AppImage, with a setup window that asks for your disc the first time, is coming to this release shortly. **Mac:** build it from this release's source: `scripts/builder/build.sh "/path/to/GZLE01.iso" --platform macos --out build/macos`. Your saves in `~/Library/Application Support/BlueWake` are kept. ### What's new **Faster** - Elliott Tate's lean block copies are now how BlueWake builds the game: 5 to 12% faster, most on slower CPUs (measured by pdale-boop). - Windows: Elliott's draw fusion sends the graphics card about a tenth as many draws, so busy places like Forest Haven, Hyrule and boss fights no longer wait on graphics. On slower CPUs he measured 30 to 60% more frames there. - Faster single-precision float loads in the game code, also from Elliott. - Linux: the game compiles about twice as fast when you build it, and runs up to 10% faster on slower CPUs (pdale-boop). - Building your own copy is faster everywhere: the optimization training takes about 12 minutes instead of 30 (pdale-boop), and a second build into the same folder works again. **Smoother** - With Smooth Motion on, CPUs with 8 threads or more no longer drop to 30 for seconds after a hitch. **Controllers** - A controller that's already plugged in when BlueWake starts now gets the smooth stick and plays as player 1 (#138). - With a GameCube adapter, press a button on your controller and it becomes player 1, even if it isn't in port 1 (#155). - Rumble only shakes the controller you're playing with (#190). - The left stick works at the Pictobox's "keep this picture?" and in the gallery (#191). - New, optional: hold the right-stick click and move it up or down to zoom the camera, under Controls (thanks to cforain). **Fixes and more** - A rare crash that could stop the game anywhere (`unmapped pc=0x8180fff0`), tracked down by pdale-boop. - Windows: the window opens where you left it (thanks to saulob), and portable mode keeps your remaps and window layout in its own folder (#64). - You can place the FPS counter in a corner, under Display (thanks to saulob). - The session log names the graphics API in use, and Linux says when it fell back to a much slower renderer because Vulkan is missing. ### How it was checked The Windows build was made on my PC (Ryzen 7 5700U) from my own disc, and it starts, runs and quits cleanly there. Every change passed the Windows and Linux builds and tests. The speed changes were measured before they went in: lean blocks by pdale-boop on Windows and Linux, including a 15-minute play session, and draw fusion by Elliott, who checked that the game plays the same. I built and checked the iPhone and iPad app without game code, the source and the PadMint recipe on a Mac. I haven't yet played this build with a controller on every platform, so if something doesn't work on your setup, please tell me. ### Known problems - Draw fusion is on for Windows only for now. On Linux and Mac you can try it with `DOL_GX_FUSE=1`; tell me how it looks. - Busy scenes can still run below 30 FPS on slower CPUs

[Details](https://github.com/kolbicz/Cyanide#supported-devices) # Cyanide 1.16.0 Supervised mode, Gravity Lite without the Installer, and live tweaks in the background again. ## New - **Supervision** (Settings → System → Supervision): Activate marks the device as supervised, with "Cyanide" as the organization, so configuration profiles with supervised-only restrictions can be installed. Only the flag is set: no device management is involved and nothing is restricted by itself. - Takes effect right away (reopen Settings) and persists across reboots. - Deactivate puts the previous state back. A device supervised by a real organization is left alone. - **Gravity Lite** now has Activate / Deactivate buttons on its Settings page and is no longer an Installer package. A full exploit run is only offered when there is no saved kernel access. ## Fixes - **Live tweaks run in the background again**: Gravity Lite, StatBar, NSBar, NiceBar Lite, Axon Lite and LiveWP keep updating while Cyanide is in the background (needs "Keep app alive in background", on by default). - **Location Services control** (Control Center / Shortcuts): switching it while a live tweak runs no longer crashes SpringBoard. - **iPad Dock with SBCustomizer's extra Dock icons** ([#12](https://github.com/kolbicz/Cyanide/issues/12)): the iPad Dock is resized after SBCustomizer changes the Dock, so an extra icon is no longer squeezed in at the left edge. ## Removed - **Sandbox escape** launch option. The File Browser, Cache Cleaner, System Info and the Lara tools lift the sandbox themselves when opened, so runs no longer spend a step on it. ## About A18 / M4 On A18 / M4 devices a run has about a 50/50 chance of rebooting the device (a kernel "panic") instead of succeeding — a known limit of these chips that can't be fully fixed. It's a coin flip, so if it reboots, just try again; a few attempts usually gets there. Once a run works, it stays working until your next restart. If you keep hitting panics, Settings → Launch Options has four knobs for the A18 chain — exploit path (pe_v3 default, pe_v1 / pe_v2), memory shaping, interleaved search and bounded search. Defaults are unchanged in this release; other combinations may do better on your device. Each applies to the next fresh run.

[Details](https://github.com/kolbicz/Cyanide#supported-devices) # Cyanide 1.14.0 Font Overwrite, including the Lock Screen clock, and SpringBoard Tools that apply together with your other tweaks. ## New - **Font Overwrite** (Settings → Lara): replace the system font, its italic and monospaced variants, or the **Lock Screen clock** with a font of your own. Nothing on the sealed system volume changes, and a restart always brings the original back. **Restore** does it without a restart (the original is backed up first). - Import a `.ttf`, `.otf` or `.ttc` from Files, tap it and pick what to replace. Respring to see the change everywhere else. ## Changes - **SpringBoard Tools:** new **Apply with Tweaks** switch. Your SpringBoard Tools look is applied in every Apply Tweaks run too, e.g. after a respring. ## Fixes - **SpringBoard Tools:** with Folder set to Disabled, folder backgrounds no longer come back while you swipe between Home Screen pages. ## About A18 / M4 On A18 / M4 devices a run has about a 50/50 chance of rebooting the device (a kernel "panic") instead of succeeding — a known limit of these chips that can't be fully fixed. versions.localizedDescription: ## 测试版更新日志 比较范围：v1.34.1 → 5750d32 ### 新增 - 桌面端支持从账号最近发布的动态、评论中识别手机型号和系统信息，自动用于请求设备配置；无可用记录时使用 iPhone 18 Pro Max 兼容模板。 - 设备设置页展示自动识别的机型及来源。自动配置保留手动指纹和已保存的数盟设备 ID，切换账号时重新识别。 - 搜索分类支持拖动排序，并可收起不常用栏目。 - 无图模式新增详情页图片显示开关。 - 新增浅色界面底色自定义和动态背景图显示开关。 - 话题页新增我的点评卡片。 - 设置页新增“液态玻璃”总开关，默认关闭，可统一控制首页和话题导航的液态玻璃效果。 ### 优化 - 移动首页滚动时可自动收起搜索栏和底部导航；详情页底栏支持随滚动隐藏。 - 优化移动端上传、下载布局，并增加 CDN 上传入口。 - 优化首页与话题的沉浸式导航，适配 Android 和 iOS 安全区，并统一上下导航的玻璃效果。 - 优化设置页窄屏和大字体下的布局。 - 设置中心统一使用一个“设置”标签，切换菜单不再新增标签，返回时打开最近访问的栏目；已有固定和收藏的设置标签自动合并。 - 隐藏桌面设置内容区与侧栏重复的栏目标题，保留说明和功能分组。 ### 修复 - 修复私信列表中同一联系人可能重复显示的问题，覆盖缓存恢复、刷新及分页加载场景。 - 修复已安装测试版选择稳定版更新渠道时，错误展示旧稳定版更新日志、发布日期和 Release 链接的问题。 - 修正关于页的版本类型与更新渠道说明，避免测试版安装包被误认为稳定版。 - 修复手机快捷入口图标缺失。 - 修复系统榜首屏内容不足时不继续加载下一页，以及双列瀑布流滚动抽动、短列加载不及时的问题。 - 修复切换应用窗口标签后话题列表意外刷新的问题。 - 修复头条刷新和分页时游标传递异常。 - 修复私信图片预览及输入区高度调节问题。 - 修复详情评论点赞状态的主题色显示，以及话题简介文字与背景对比度不足的问题。

NBA Showtime now uses the arcade/MAME edition on iOS and Windows, replacing the previous PlayStation edition. Import your own nbashowt.zip and matching nbashowt.chd; game data is not included. Showtime iPhone changes: - Move emulation off the UI thread and pace it using a monotonic deadline. - Batch two signature-checked MIPS polling/copy loops while preserving guest cycles, RAM semantics and interrupt boundaries. - Bound queued audio latency; fade starvation/recovery and transition across dropped audio to reduce crackles. - Reduce CRT drawable workload under thermal pressure. CRT remains on by default and can be toggled. Includes all pending source changes for the other four ports, including their rendering, camera, CRT and version-resource updates. Downloads: - SSF2T 0.4.2, UMK3 0.4.2, Slam n Jam 96 0.4.2, THPS2 0.4.3, NBA Showtime 0.4.6 unsigned iOS IPAs. - NativePorts-Windows-x64.zip contains all five Windows builds and required DLLs. - SHA256SUMS.txt provides download checksums. IPAs require signing before installation. Validation: iOS and Windows builds passed; 15,000 randomized MIPS-loop comparisons passed with sanitizers; audio, worker-thread, game import, rendering and camera regression tests passed. The latest separate Showtime iPhone test build was reported to run well by the device owner. Sustained coverage of every scene and physical four-player testing remain pending. Showtime arcade widescreen projection is not implemented; native arcade proportions are retained.

NBA Showtime (PlayStation USA) joins the four existing ports. All five iOS apps and Windows executables are version 0.3.0. Changes: - SSF2T: fixed 512-column widescreen output prevents camera-dependent resizing. Unsupported stage edges are clipped inside the fixed canvas and filled with colored margins; scenery is not mirrored. - Slam 'n Jam '96: extend the SLES-00076 game's crowd/court clipping checks, rather than only widening the GPU canvas. Original interior pixels and HUD are preserved. No coin prompts; Restart Game remains the console action. - UMK3: extend solid background/gradient clears into the extra columns before drawing foreground scenery, fixing the rectangular gap reproduced in Scorpion's Lair. - THPS2: keep the gameplay HUD in the centered original 4:3 area. Increase the normal follow-camera offset by 25% through a guarded boot-time instruction patch, verified on the USA executable. Black letterbox bars and CRT toggle are retained. - NBA Showtime: supplied PlayStation USA BIN support, four-player multitap, Hangtime-style controls/UI, centered HUD and expanded gameplay canvas, CRT enabled by default with on/off controls. - Include THPS2's Windows C++ runtime DLLs and version all five builds consistently. Downloads: - NativePorts-Windows-x64.zip: all five Windows games. Extract it and keep every DLL beside its EXE. - Five unsigned IPAs: sign with your sideloading tool. Keep existing bundle identifiers to preserve app data. - SHA256SUMS.txt: checksums for the downloadable builds. Game files and signing credentials are not included. NBA Showtime needs the extracted raw PlayStation MODE2/2352 BIN named nbashowt.bin, not its archive or an arcade ROM. Validation: all ten platform builds passed; Apple/SDL virtual-controller tests, shader compilation, texture-cache checks, rendering helper regressions and local gameplay captures passed. Local captures covered SSF2T camera limits, Slam court pans, UMK3 Scorpion's Lair, THPS2 Hangar, and NBA Showtime gameplay/toggle/HUD. This is not complete stage coverage or physical iPhone/Windows multiplayer validation. THPS2 iOS still uses the CPU interpreter; this release does not claim a verified frame-rate improvement. Some Slam camera angles can still reveal the finite arena's dark exterior.

SSF2T and Slam n Jam 0.2.2 iOS and Windows builds passed. iOS IPAs are unsigned; sign/install with ESign, keeping the existing bundle identifiers. Slam n Jam: startup asks for keyboard 1 or controller Start, with no coin prompt. Restart reads RESTART GAME. PS1 Select is available as Select (keyboard Tab, controller View); old settings migrate. Native gameplay canvas expands from 320 to 426 columns instead of stretching. Original-size sprites, text and HUD remain centered; textures live in original VRAM and expanded framebuffers use separate banks. CRT behavior is unchanged. SSF2T: reflected edge artwork removed. The visible gameplay window narrows symmetrically as the camera approaches finite stage boundaries, returning to the original 384 columns at either limit. It expands away from those limits. Menus keep their original proportions centered in a 512-column frame with colored sides. Validation: iOS and Windows builds, controller suite, canvas isolation and stage-boundary tests passed. Real Slam gameplay toggled 320 -> 426 -> 320 columns; all 81,920 pixels of the central original view matched the same saved frame exactly. Real SSF2T gameplay captures returned to 384 columns at both edges, and menu captures were 512 columns with colored margins. Device-specific iPhone and Windows gameplay still needs retesting. No game files or game screenshots are included. SSF2T and Slam n Jam are version 0.2.2. The unchanged THPS2 and UMK3 version 0.2.1 builds are also included here. Download NativePorts-Windows-x64.zip for all four current Windows builds; the smaller SSF2T-SlamJam96 ZIP contains only those two games. BUILD-VERSIONS.txt inside the complete ZIP identifies every game version.

NativePorts 0.2.0 includes Super Street Fighter II Turbo, Ultimate Mortal Kombat 3, Slam ’n Jam ’96 and Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 2 for iOS and Windows. - Uses the supplied game artwork for each iOS app and Windows executable/window icon. Keeps unique bundle IDs unchanged to preserve installed game data. - Adds game-specific widescreen patches for SSF2T, UMK3 and Slam ’n Jam ’96, alongside the existing Flycast widescreen patch for THPS2. Widescreen can be toggled in display settings. - Updates aspect-ratio handling and NewPixie CRT rendering to preserve picture edges. CRT filtering remains enabled by default and can be disabled. - Refreshes cached core sources before builds so source changes rebuild the embedded engine. - Includes touch controls and remappable multiplayer controller support on both platforms. Download one unsigned IPA per game and sign it with your sideloading tool. For Windows, extract NativePorts-Windows-x64.zip and keep each EXE beside its SDL2.dll. Use your own game files; ROMs, disc images and signing credentials are not included. Known limitations: THPS2 on iOS uses an interpreter and may run below full speed. Slam ’n Jam ’96 can leave dark corners in some widescreen camera angles. NBA Showtime remains frontend-only and is not included. Validation: all four iOS build logs report success; Windows binaries were packaged from the latest local builds. Virtual controller tests passed for all five frontends, along with ROM-import checks, basketball action tests and both THPS2 texture-cache configurations. These checks do not establish full-speed performance or physical multiplayer operation on every device. SHA256SUMS.txt contains asset checksums.

Super Street Fighter II Turbo 0.1.1, Ultimate Mortal Kombat 3 0.1.1, Slam 'n Jam '96 0.1.1 and Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 0.1.9 for iOS and Windows. Unsigned IPAs for sideloading (ESign, AltStore, SideStore, Sideloadly) and a Windows x64 package. No game files are included; see the README for what you need.
