# Theft4 0.3 — direct Metal and a rebuilt rendering path Apple version **0.3.0**, build **123**, launcher label **0.3**. Source and the full engineering record are published on GitHub main. The [0.3 GitHub release](https://github.com/KoreanSeats1/Theft4/releases/tag/v0.3) includes the unsigned ARM64 IPA and its checksum. TestFlight publication is separate. The full engineering changelog is [recorded here](https://github.com/KoreanSeats1/Theft4/blob/v0.3/CHANGELOG.md#03--direct-metal-rebuilt-geometry-and-a-faster-native-rendering-path--2026-10-06). 0.3 is the largest rendering change in Theft4 so far. The running game now sends its prepared frames directly to Metal. This includes the actual city, characters, lighting, effects and presentation, rather than just the separate Metal Lab. The renderer and its CPU preparation, resource lifetimes and upload caches have been substantially rebuilt around Apple's graphics API. On the M5 iPad, the tester reports a huge improvement and very good gameplay at the selected native resolution, with a remaining spike that now recovers. Subsequent build 122 testing was also reported as excellent. The latest retrieved native log confirms a 2416×1359 internal/output target with no upscaling. This is much closer to the desired console experience. It does not establish a locked 30 FPS in every scene, uninterrupted long-session stability, or equivalent performance on other hardware. The engineering target remains under 30 ms of frame work, leaving margin inside the 33.3 ms interval for 30 FPS. ## The direct Metal change The previous production rendering route used the GTA IV frontend, Vulkan and MoltenVK before reaching Metal. 0.3 introduces a live Metal worker, native render passes, native resource bindings, completion-owned frame storage and direct CAMetalLayer presentation. Normal Metal gameplay does not realize its draws through the Vulkan provider or presenter. Game shaders are prepared offline from the project's stock shader corpus. Their constant banks and reflected texture/sampler fetches become explicit Metal bindings. The game no longer needs to compile that corpus through a live Vulkan translation path to produce its Metal draws. Pipeline variants and Metal driver compilation can still require work when a new scene is encountered. The game remains an ahead-of-time recompilation of the supported Xbox 360 release. Its compiled ARM64 code still uses the compatibility runtime for the title's memory, service and calling conventions. This release does not replace all game logic with handwritten native code, rewrite physics or traffic, or turn the project into a PC source port. Legacy Vulkan code and libraries remain in the build for comparison and compatibility; direct rendering is a runtime route, not a claim that the application has no Vulkan symbols or dependencies. ## Rendering correctness and clarity - Complete ordered frames now include the game's render passes, color resolves, depth handoffs, reflections and host effects. Draw order and required prior attachment contents are preserved across internal submissions. - The port handles reversed viewport depth, the negative-one-to-one vertex depth convention, attachmentless draws, depth-only pipelines, per-instance stream 16, buffered/indexed rectangles and rotating output drawables. - Packed lighting aliases and the title's float-pair multiple render targets retain their intended channel masks and storage roles. GPU-produced surfaces are distinct from immutable uploaded textures. - Sampling preserves mip ranges, row/plane pitches, layers, cube faces and channel swizzles. Reflection updates wait for valid written content rather than making an entire otherwise valid scene fail. - Blending, alpha discard, sample coverage, output scaling and clamping are checked against the game shader contract. Normal presentation uses GPU textures directly. - Color targets use render-appropriate private storage without unnecessary usage flags that defeated compr

On a limited-memory device, settings that would create unnecessary rendering or memory pressure are constrained at launch and whenever graphics settings are changed: - 1080p and Native requests are capped at 900p with FSR and fixed 1080p output; - existing lower 540p and 720p selections remain lower rather than being raised; - original shadow size, optimized draw distance, original model detail and reflections are used; - additional edge smoothing, anisotropic filtering, motion blur, depth of field, and the optional FSR sharpening boost are disabled; - launcher choices above the supported ceiling are visibly unavailable. versions.localizedDescription: # Skate 3 Recompiled v2.7.1 — iOS iOS skipped a release. Everything Android got in v0.2.0 is here, plus two iOS-specific defaults. 24 engine commits and 17 SDK commits since v2.6.3. ## Put any button anywhere Full controller remapping, on the Controls page under **Button Mapping**. Sixteen inputs — the four face buttons, both bumpers, both triggers, both stick clicks, Back, Start and the four D-pad directions — can each be moved to any of the others. Your mapping is saved and survives an update. The sticks themselves are not remapped; Swap Sticks and Invert Camera Y already cover that. ## Three bugs that were costing you frames **Touching the frame-rate row uncapped the game.** One setting's name was a prefix of another's (`..._fps_cap` inside `..._fps_cap_auto`), so changing the Framerate Cap row erased the shipped cap entirely, on every launch after you touched that row. The game then ran the guest loop uncapped. On Android that also meant rendering roughly twice the frames the panel could show and dumping the rest as heat, which is what "runs at 60, drops after a few minutes" was there; iOS presents through FIFO, so the cost here is wasted work rather than heat. **"The frame rate is fine but it feels like slow motion."** Skate 3 advances exactly one refresh period of simulation per rendered frame, however long that frame took, so a 33 ms frame runs the game at half speed. The ceiling that lets a frame advance more than one period (skate3_frame_advance_cap) had been compiled for Switch only — iOS and Android, the two platforms whose frames overrun the period most, never got it. It is compiled in on iOS now. Being straight about this one: the clamp is in and reachable, but raising it was measured as changing nothing on hardware, so treat it as a lever that now exists rather than a fix you are guaranteed to feel. **A profiler was running in every build.** A per-packet GPU timer took two clock reads and two atomic increments on every command packet — around 1.7 million clock reads a second on the busiest thread — whether or not anyone was profiling. It is off unless you ask for it. ## First launch could come up blank Roughly one clean install in ten reached the setup screen with an empty options list and no way forward. Parts of a screen drawn once while their shaders were still compiling were skipped and never came back — and the difficulty prompt is drawn exactly once. Shader compilation now stays synchronous through the cold-boot frontend, so nothing can draw before it is ready. ## New in Settings Eleven new rows, most of them aimed at buying frames back on a phone: - **3D Scene Resolution** — Full / 75% / 67% / 50% / 40%, separate from UI sharpness - **Draw Distance** — now goes down to Quarter and Eighth - **NPC Update Rate** and **World Update Rate** - **Pedestrians & Traffic**, **Movable Props**, **Other Skaters** — stop the world spawning crowds you are not looking at (all three need a restart) - **Vegetation**, **Hair Detail**, **Water Effects**, **Draw Batching** - **Framerate Cap** — 40, 45 and 50 added (40 divides 120 Hz, 45 divides 90 Hz) - **FPS Percentiles** — the 1% low and p95/p99 next to the average (darchap's, see Credit). Known limitation on the three population cuts: they remove the bodies, not the gameplay objects behind them, so you may still hear pedestrians, traffic and other skaters you cannot see. Being worked on. The average is exactly the statistic that hides a stutter: a steady 60 and a 60 that drops four frames a second read the same. ## Two changed defaults on iOS - **Draw distance now ships at Half.** The static world is roughly 750 of the 765 things drawn in a frame, so it is the only content lever with real weight behind it. The trade is real: props, street furniture and foliage pop in closer than they did in 2.6.3. **Settings > Video > Draw Distance > Original** puts it back. **This applies to new installs only.** If you are updating, your existing draw distance is kept exactly as it is — the

> **Superseded by [v2.7.1](https://github.com/andrewnakas/skate3-ios-setup/releases/latest).** > This build shipped the in-app title-update install, which still works exactly as described below. > It also shipped the Framerate Cap row that silently erased the 60 fps cap on every later launch — fixed in 2.7.1. ### Original v2.6.3 notes **The title update can now be installed from inside the app.** Previously iOS could do neither half of this: the "select a file" route went through the system document picker, which does not work under TrollStore or on a jailbreak, and the download button was never shown at all. Players who had just installed from a disc image were left able to install the game and then unable to install the update it requires. Both routes work now: - **Download it in the app.** Tap "Install the title update" and then Download. It fetches the 1.7 MB package and installs it, with no computer involved. - **Or copy it in yourself.** A package already sitting in your Skate 3 folder is found automatically, the same way disc images have been found since 2.6.0. No picker, no file browser. **A home screen on iOS.** The app now opens on a launcher instead of straight into the game: Play, install from a disc image, install the title update, choose a map pack, and save a diagnostic report you can share from the Files app. Every row returns to it, so you can install a disc, then the update, then pick a pack in one sitting. **Settings now stick.** Twenty-four rows were being forced back to their defaults at every launch - resolution, V-Sync, MSAA, shadows, ambient occlusion, bloom, sun shafts, draw distance, the frame cap, and the audio and interface rows. The menu wrote your choice to disk and startup overwrote it on the way back in, so the rows looked broken. Audio Buffer Size in particular simply never applied. Opening and closing the settings menu also used to freeze the per-device memory budgets at whatever that one launch happened to pick; it no longer writes rows you did not touch. **Map pack names in other languages.** A pack built for one market carries English text and leaves the other languages empty, and the game was showing those empty slots - an unnamed entry in the map list and raw identifiers where level names belong, reported as the DLC maps not loading in French or Spanish. Names now fall back to English instead of coming back blank. This is fixed in the game rather than in the packs, so it applies to every pack you already have. Requires iOS 16.0 or later and a 6-core device. You still supply your own copy of the game.

> **Superseded by [v2.6.0](https://github.com/andrewnakas/skate3-ios-setup/releases/latest).** > This build slows down on mission completion and replay screens, and a long > session decays toward single-digit frame rates. Use the latest release. ### Original v2.5.0 notes # Skate 3 for iOS — v2.5.0 Hey — this one's a big catch-up. The last public release was **v2.4.0**, and everything from 2.4.1 through 2.4.7 got built and then never actually shipped, so all of it lands here at once along with the new stuff. Install it with AltStore or SideStore. The `.ipa` doesn't contain the game — you bring your own copy of Skate 3 and it walks you through installing it the first time you launch. --- The headline: **the game used to measure itself while you played, and now it doesn't.** Every build up to this point shipped with the performance tools running — a frame-timing summary, a present-cadence tracker, and a ten-clock breakdown of literally every frame that went to the screen. The lines they wrote to the log were cheap. The bookkeeping behind them ran on every single frame whether anything got printed or not, and everybody paid for it just to play the game. That's all off now. It didn't get deleted, though — that detail is what makes a bug report useful. It moved behind a **Diagnostics switch in Settings → System**. If something goes wrong and someone asks you for a log, flip it on, play until it happens again, and send the log. No special build, no config files to hand-edit. **The settings menu asks before it closes the game now.** On iOS, applying a setting that needs a restart means quitting — that's genuinely the only way some of them can take effect — and it used to just do it, instantly, the moment you picked it. Worse, it was also wired to a bare button on a controller, so one stray press and your session was gone. It asks now, and "Keep Playing" is the option your thumb lands on by default. **And the buttons are actually sized for fingers.** Those little circles either side of each setting were built for a mouse pointer. On a phone they worked out to about two millimetres across — roughly a third of what a touch target is supposed to be — and the invisible margin around them didn't scale at all. They are more than twice the size now, with a proper margin, and the rows and category buttons grew to match. **A Potato preset**, under Settings → Video → Preset, sitting below Performance. It gives the picture up rather than trimming it: no shadows at all, no ambient occlusion, bloom or sun shafts, and half the draw distance. On a phone this is the setting with the most room behind it, because the emulated CPU is what issues all the draw calls, so cutting them lands on emulation rather than on the GPU. **Logs got a lot quieter.** The content scan used to fire off about fifty warnings every boot about files that were completely fine, which buried anything that actually mattered. A log now leads with the build version and reports real problems. --- ### Everything from the releases that never went out **Frame rate** - iPhones with ProMotion displays (13 Pro and newer) were running the entire game at **30 fps**. That's fixed — they run at 60 now. Touching the screen also halved the frame rate on those phones, which is fixed too. - *Every* iPhone was running at **half the frame rate it should have been.** The graphics layer was encoding each frame's work inline while it submitted it, which serialised two things that are supposed to overlap. Measured on a real device: 30 fps to 60. **Freezes and crashes** - The game could go permanently black while the audio just kept playing. The unmodified wrapper fails the truncated-file case. This establishes the extraction repair, not physical-device or provider-specific picker acceptance, gameplay, audio, or performance.

# Playport 0.3.3: JIT your way **Playport now works with the JIT tools you already use.** Its built-in JIT helper is still the easiest way to play. But if you already enable JIT with **StikDebug**, or run your apps inside **LiveContainer**, Playport now takes JIT from them too. You no longer need Playport's own pairing. ## Highlights ### 🔌 Choose where JIT comes from A new **JIT method** setting in **Settings › Setup check** (or press **X** on the setup checklist's first step) offers three ways: | Method | What happens when you press Play | | --- | --- | | **Built-in** (default) | Playport's own helper enables JIT, as before. No other app, no app switch. | | **StikDebug** | Playport opens StikDebug, which enables JIT and brings you back to the game. | | **Another app** | Playport waits for JIT from the app you use, such as LiveContainer's *Launch with JIT*. | StikDebug and other apps use StikDebug's standard **`universal.js`** script. Playport's JIT already speaks its protocol, so there is no custom script to install. ### 📦 LiveContainer support LiveContainer can't start Playport's built-in helper, so Playport now notices when it runs inside LiveContainer and hides the Built-in method. Two ways to play: 1. **Launch with JIT** (recommended): in LiveContainer, set the JIT enabler to StikDebug with `universal.js`, and turn on *Launch with JIT* for Playport. Playport finds JIT already there, so Play doesn't wait for it. 2. **StikDebug from Playport**: choose StikDebug as the JIT method and turn on *Use LiveContainer's Bundle ID* in LiveContainer's settings. ### 🧭 A setup that fits your method - With StikDebug or another app, Playport's own **pairing is no longer a setup step**, and a missing pairing never stops a game. - LocalDevVPN is skipped too when another app brings JIT. StikDebug still uses it. - While a game waits for JIT, the launch screen says what it is waiting for. If JIT doesn't arrive, it tells you what to check for the method you chose. ## Good to know - **One game per launch.** After a game, Playport normally restarts itself so the next one gets fresh JIT. That restart needs Playport's pairing, and inside LiveContainer it isn't possible at all. In those cases Playport asks you to close it and launch it again (with JIT) before the next game. - **Built-in is unchanged** and still the default. If it works for you, there is nothing to do. - **Not tested with StikDebug or LiveContainer yet.** Playport is tested on one phone (iOS 27.0), which has neither. Built-in was checked with Hollow Knight. If you play through StikDebug or LiveContainer, please tell us how it goes. Thanks to the player who asked for this: *"in app JIT enabling is cool and all, but it doesn't work under LiveContainer"*. Now it should: let us know. Everything else is as in 0.3.2.

# Playport 0.3.0: 32-bit games **32-bit Windows games now run on your iPhone.** Until now Playport ran only 64-bit games. 0.3.0 adds a full 32-bit runtime with Direct3D 9 graphics on Apple's GPU, and **Portal 2** is the first 32-bit game that plays: menus, test chambers, both portals, sound, controller, saves and Steam Cloud. Everything runs locally on a non-jailbroken iPhone: no streaming, no remake, no PC. ## Highlights ### 🧩 32-bit Windows games - 32-bit (x86) games run next to 64-bit ones, from the same Library and the same Play button. Nothing to set up. - iOS keeps the lowest 4 GB of memory to itself, which is exactly where a 32-bit game has to live. Playport gives each 32-bit game its own 4 GB window higher up and translates every memory access on the fly, so the game never notices. ### 🎨 Direct3D 9 on the iPhone's GPU, through KosmicKrisp - Direct3D 9 runs on DXVK, then Vulkan, then Metal through **KosmicKrisp**, Mesa's Vulkan driver for Apple GPUs, ported to iOS for Playport. - 32-bit games pick Vulkan automatically. Game options show "Default · Vulkan". - KosmicKrisp keeps its compiled shaders on disk, so the second launch of a game reuses them instead of compiling again. ### 🌀 Portal 2 - Plays at **about 60 FPS at 720p**. A 5-minute play with portals, tunnels, a death and a reload averaged 58.4 FPS. - A 95-minute session with saving and loading ran without a crash. After a long session the phone gets warm, and Portal 2 then runs at about 50 FPS. - Saves sync with Steam Cloud, so you can carry on where you left off on your PC. ### ⚡ Faster 32-bit games - x87 floating-point math, which older 32-bit games use heavily, now runs at the CPU's native 64-bit precision, as Valve's Proton does on ARM64. Portal 2's main thread does about 40 % less work and the CPU draws about 40 % less power, so the phone stays cooler and holds 60 FPS for longer. ## Fixes and improvements - Controllers work in games that bring their own copy of XInput (Portal 2 does). - Steam Cloud: Portal 2's saves upload again, and a file Steam refuses no longer stops the whole sync. - Games that ask for Tahoma show their text: Playport now ships fallback Tahoma fonts. - A new opening animation while your stores load, and a launch that dives into the game's art. The game then fades in at its own size. - A game's art fills the screen on its page and during its launch. ## Known limitations - Portal 2 is the only 32-bit game tested so far. Other 32-bit Direct3D 9 games use the same route, but expect rough edges. Please tell us how they run. - 32-bit games run only on Vulkan. Choosing DXMT for one, on its page or globally, stops it from starting. - Expect short hitches when a level loads and the first time you see a new effect. - In long sessions the iPhone heats up and lowers its clock speeds, and frame rates drop. ## Install Download `Playport-0.3.0.ipa` and sideload it with your own Apple ID, keeping the increased memory limit and the JIT helper extension. If you have an earlier version, install over it: your games, saves and Steam login stay. Bring your own games from Steam. Filter by All, Installed or Steam, and tell copies of the same game from different stores apart. ## Fixes and improvements - B takes you back to where you were. - The Home banner opens the game's page. - Long game names fit on the launch screen.
## Playport 0.1.0 First experimental release: Windows games on your iPhone. No jailbreak or streaming. Download the IPA and sideload it onto your iPhone.

# Playport 0.5.0: World of Warcraft, Red Dead Redemption 2, The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered and touch controls
<!-- date: 2026-11-02 -->

**This is the big one. World of Warcraft is on your iPhone.** Install it straight from
Blizzard through Playport's new **Battle.net** store, sign in and step into Azeroth. **Red
Dead Redemption 2** rides out of Arthur's cabin, **The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered**
plays in Kaer Morhen, and **no controller is needed any more**: on-screen touch controls
with three layouts, a full layout editor, a touch keyboard, controller mapping and gyro
aim. Add a redesigned Library, a performance overlay and Vulkan for every game.

**Updated IPA (2 November 2026).** The 0.5.0 IPA was replaced with a build that adds three
fixes:

- 32-bit games that unpack their own code at start-up (The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth, The
  Witcher 2) no longer crash before their first frame.
- Playport's Steam client now gives a game Steam's ownership ticket, so The Witcher 2's DRM

## Highlights

### ⚔️ World of Warcraft, from Battle.net
**Battle.net is now a store in Playport**, next to Steam, GOG and Epic Games, and World of
Warcraft shows in everyone's Library. No Battle.net app and no sign-in in Playport: pick
the game, press Install, and Playport downloads it from Blizzard's own servers.

- **Retail, Classic, Classic Era and Classic Anniversary**, each with a region picker (US,
  Europe, Korea or Taiwan; your phone's region by default) and a language. Playport checks
  the free space before it starts and installs through Downloads, with pause, resume and
  cancel.
- **Always up to date:** every Play checks for a new build first and updates through
  Downloads, then plays. *Check for update* sits on the game's page too.
- **The game signs itself in**, as on a PC. The in-game menu's new **Type text** opens a
  field over the game for your email, password and authenticator code, with paste and
  AutoFill.
- **It plays.** In our testing World of Warcraft reaches its login screen within about
  45 seconds of Play and runs in the world at **55–60 FPS**.
- **Your game, untouched:** Playport runs Blizzard's own Windows client through its
  translator and changes none of the game's files and none of its code in memory. Before
  the first Play it tells you plainly that Blizzard does not support Playport.

![The Library's Battle.net store with World of Warcraft](https://playport.dev/screenshots/library-battlenet.webp)

### 🤠 Red Dead Redemption 2 rides
Press Play and Rockstar's own launcher starts, signs in, hands the game its ticket and gets
out of the way. Social Club runs on Rockstar's own components, so the game stays signed in
and saves as it should. One press on Story and you are in Arthur's cabin, on the frontier,
on a phone.

![Arthur Morgan in a winter coat on a snowy cabin porch, snow-covered pines beyond](https://playport.dev/screenshots/rdr2.webp)

### 🐺 The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered plays
The remastered 4.x build of The Witcher 3 used to stop the moment it started: it needs
AVX instructions the phone could not offer and asks for far more memory space than an
iPhone app gets. Playport now handles both, and Geralt is back in Kaer Morhen, on the
game's Direct3D 12 renderer. The classic 1.32 build still plays as before.

![Geralt walking through a hall of Kaer Morhen past a lit fireplace](https://playport.dev/screenshots/witcher3-remastered.webp)

### 🎮 On-screen controls: play with nothing but the phone
No controller? Playport draws its **on-screen controls** over the game. Connect a controller
and they step aside; disconnect it and they come back (*Settings › Controls*: Automatic,
Always or Never).

- **Three layouts, plus Off:** **Gamepad** (sticks, d-pad, A/B/X/Y, bumpers, triggers, View
  and Menu), **Keyboard & mouse** (a W A S D stick, drag anywhere free to look, key caps
  around your thumb) and **Point & click** (tap to click or use it as a trackpad, with a
  magnifier for small targets, plus right click, hover, scroll, keys and Esc).
- **A three-finger tap** anywhere opens Playport's in-game menu, with any layout. The first
  time the controls appear on their own, a toast says so.
- **The layout editor:** add, move, resize, duplicate and remove controls on a grid with
  snapping guides, undo, reset and switch presets, by touch or with a controller, over the
  paused game or from *Game options › Controls*. Each game keeps its own layout and its own
  opacity.
- **A suggested starting layout:** a game that never asks for a controller in its first
  20 seconds is offered Keyboard & mouse, once.
- **A touch keyboard** over the game, with F keys, arrows and sticky Shift, Ctrl and Alt,
  for consoles, names and the keys a layout lacks.
- **Any controller as a keyboard and mouse:** *Game options › Controls › Controller* maps
  every button, stick, trigger and gyro to a controller input, a key with modifiers, a
  mouse button, mouse movement or the wheel, or a Playport action. Pick **As a controller**,
  **As keyboard & mouse** or **Custom**.
- **Gyro aim:** aim by moving the phone, or a DualSense, DualShock 4 or Switch Pro
  controller, as the mouse or the right stick, per game, with sensitivity, smoothing and a
  test area to try it before you play.

![The layout editor over World of Warcraft, editing the Keyboard & mouse layout](https://playport.dev/screenshots/touch-editor.webp)

![World of Warcraft on a ship's deck with a blue dragon mount, with the on-screen Gamepad layout](https://playport.dev/screenshots/wow-gamepad.webp)

### 📚 A redesigned Library
The stores are now **a column of icons down the Library's left**: All, Steam, GOG, Epic
Games and Battle.net, every one always there (a store you are signed out of is dimmed).
The chosen store's name and game count sit above the grid, and **Installed only** narrows
any of them with one tap. With a controller, press left from the first column to reach the
stores, or step through them from anywhere with LT and RT.

![The Library with All games and the store column](https://playport.dev/screenshots/library-0.5.webp)

### 📊 A performance overlay
A small pill at the top of the game shows the **frame rate, the frame time and your phone's
thermal state**. Turn it on from the in-game menu or *Settings › Graphics*, and it stays on
for every game. It replaces Apple's Metal HUD, which cost CPU time on every frame.

## Also new
- **Vulkan is every game's graphics backend.** Direct3D 9, 10, 11 and 12 now run on Vulkan
  over Metal by default. DXMT stays one choice away in *Settings › Graphics › Direct3D* or
  on the game's page.
- **Quicker launches:** shaders are compiled faster for Metal on iOS 27, and what the
  graphics backends and the code translator have done is kept on disk, so a second launch
  skips the first one's work. *Settings › Storage › Shader cache* shows the space and
  clears it.
- **OpenGL games run**, through Mesa's Zink on Vulkan, in 64-bit and 32-bit games alike.
- **More room for big games:** each Play's memory is planned from your phone's memory and
  the game's needs, freed memory is reused, and *Settings › Graphics › Donor memory*
  (Auto by default) lets a game use more than the app alone could hold.
- **Steam for 32-bit games too:** Playport's own Steam client now serves 32-bit games the
  same sign-in, ownership check and online tickets as 64-bit ones. **Repair** fetches
  missing Steamworks Shared files.
- **Games get what they need, from Play:** an *Installing dependencies* step runs a game's
  own prerequisite installer once, fetches Steam's or GOG's redistributables, and carries
  Wine Mono for .NET games.
- **Publisher launchers:** Rockstar's launcher runs for the games that need it, and a
  game's own launcher and dialog windows show instead of an empty screen.
- **Type text** in the in-game menu sends typing, paste and AutoFill to the game's focused
  field, with a password mode.
- **Graphics choices are cleaner:** *Aspect ratio* and *Resolution* are separate, and a
  game can carry its own compatibility defaults (Super Meat Boy's 16:9, Assassin's Creed's
  Keyboard & mouse layout).
- **Screenshot** works over Vulkan games, and games that change display mode keep showing.
- **Settings scrolls** on a landscape phone; *Storage* lists Steamworks Shared, the shader
  cache and the translator's cache with their sizes.
- **Newer components:** Wine 11.20 with Valve's latest Proton Wine changes, and current
  FEX (the translator that runs x86 code on the phone), DXMT, DXVK, vkd3d-proton and Mesa.

## Good to know
- **World of Warcraft needs your Battle.net account** with an active subscription; the
  game's own login checks it. Blizzard does not support Playport, and an action on your
  account is possible: Playport asks you to accept that once before the first Play.
- **World of Warcraft is big:** retail needs about 132 GB of free space, Classic about
  80 GB and Classic Era about 5 GB. Our testing covered retail. Busy cities and raids may
  run slower than the open world.
- **Red Dead Redemption 2 and The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered push the phone to its
  limits.** Both run close to the app's memory limit and need the increased memory limit
  from your sideloader. Both heat the phone, and their frame rate drops as it warms;
  expect long loads and hitches. Red Dead Redemption 2 installs about 120 GB, and we test
  Story mode only, never Red Dead Online. In bright light some highlights look wrong (a
  white beard brim, a red ear).
- **Vulkan is the default now.** If a game looks or behaves worse than on 0.4.0, switch it
  to **DXMT** on its page (*Game options › Graphics › Direct3D*) and tell us which game.
- **On-screen controls:** without a controller, the three-finger tap is the only way into
  the in-game menu. In some games' menus a Point & click tap moves the highlight without
  opening the item (Portal 2's). A game may show controller prompts while the layout is
  Off. Gyro aim drives the game's own stick or mouse, so a game's own aim settings still
  apply.
- **Big games keep needing memory,** and a game that wants more than the phone can hold
  still ends.
- **Tested on one phone** (iOS 27.2). If a game misbehaves, *Report a problem* on its page
  shares one zip with its logs.
- Your games, saves and logins are untouched by this update; install over 0.4.0.

## Install

Download `Playport-0.5.0.ipa` and sideload it with your own Apple ID, keeping the
increased memory limit and the JIT helper extension. If you have an earlier version,
install over it: your games, saves and logins stay. Bring your own games from Steam, GOG,
Epic Games or Files, or install World of Warcraft from Battle.net.

The complete Corresponding Source of this exact build, the notices and the rebuild
instructions are attached as `Playport-0.5.0-source.tar`, `NOTICES.tar` and
`INSTALL-REBUILD.tar`. `SHA256SUMS` covers every file.

### New - **In-app JIT: no StikDebug needed.** Madeira can enable JIT by itself through a bundled helper built on StikJIT. On iOS 27 it pairs with the iPhone it runs on: in Settings › Privacy & Security › Developer Mode, tap **Pair with Madeira** and enter the PIN Madeira shows. No computer needed. On iOS 26, import a pairing file instead. The pairing is kept in the Keychain. StikDebug still works. (#127) - **Play turns JIT on for you.** If JIT is off, Play enables it and then starts the game. The button reads **Starting JIT** meanwhile. - **Madeira JIT shortcut (iOS 27, optional).** LocalDevVPN's loopback does not work over cellular data. The shortcut connects LocalDevVPN, turns Cellular Data off when there is no Wi-Fi, and puts both back once the game has started, along with any VPN you were using. Add it during setup or in Settings › JIT. - **Steam Cloud saves** for installed Steam games, on by default. Saves sync before and after you play, and the cloud copy is backed up before it is replaced. (#130) - **A controller as keyboard and mouse**, chosen per game, with a Controller binds page. DirectInput is now a per-game choice too. (#128) - **Setup** starts by installing LocalDevVPN when it is missing. It opens once more after this update, so you can pick one of the new JIT options. ### Fixed - Games start faster: Wine starts as soon as the wineserver is ready, not after a fixed 2 s. (#125) - Cuphead (#107), Nine Sols (#108) and Hades II (#119, #120) now run, and Steam app info with escaped quotes is read correctly (#118). - JIT errors now explain the problem and offer a fix: **Pair Again** or **Connect LocalDevVPN**. The error also shows on the Settings tab. ### Known issues - With Wi-Fi and Cellular Data both off, LocalDevVPN cannot connect, so JIT cannot be enabled, even with the shortcut. Connect LocalDevVPN while a network is available. ### Install - Requires **iOS 26 or later**. In-app pairing and the Madeira JIT shortcut need iOS 27. - If your sideloader asks whether to keep app extensions, keep them: Madeira's in-app JIT runs in one. - The IPA is ad-hoc signed (no certificate) and carries the app's entitlements, including the increased memory limit. Sideload it with your own Apple ID (SideStore, AltStore, Sideloadly, Plume or similar), which signs it for your device. - First-run setup walks you through JIT. Settings shows JIT and Memory+ with green checks and says **Ready to play**. ### Not included The Microsoft Visual C++ runtime DLLs are not redistributed (see `legal/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`). Building from source: `tools/fetch-vcruntime.md`. Thanks to Dan Perks ([@danperks](https://github.com/danperks)) for in-app JIT and pairing, Jesse ([@JesseLovelace](https://github.com/JesseLovelace)) for Steam Cloud saves, faster launches and the game fixes, and Nick ([@125hz](https://github.com/125hz)) for keyboard-and-mouse controllers.

### Fixed - **Direct3D 9 and Direct3D 11 games run on iOS 26 again.** The graphics layer's built-in shader library was compiled for the newest Metal version (4.1), which only iOS 27 understands, so on iOS 26 every 64-bit D3D11 game and every 32-bit D3D9 and D3D11 game failed at start-up ("This library is using language version 4.1 which is not supported on this OS"). The library now targets Metal 3.1, which every supported iOS accepts. Affects v0.1.0 and v0.1.1. (#129) ### Install - Requires **iOS 26 or later**. - The IPA is ad-hoc signed (no certificate) and carries the app's entitlements, including the increased memory limit. Sideload it with your own Apple ID (SideStore, AltStore, Sideloadly, Plume or similar), which signs it for your device. - Enable JIT with Madeira's **Enable JIT** button (StikDebug). Settings shows JIT and Memory+ with green checks and says **Ready to play**. ### Not included The Microsoft Visual C++ runtime DLLs are not redistributed (see `legal/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`). Building from source: `tools/fetch-vcruntime.md`. Thanks to Nick ([@125hz](https://github.com/125hz)) for tracking this down.

### Fixed - **Games start on iOS 26 again for free-Apple-ID installs.** Those installs get a smaller (63 GB) address map, on which Madeira's JIT memory setup failed, so every launch ended with "The session could not start". (#109) - Enabling JIT from StikDebug's own app list no longer crashes Madeira when a game starts. Madeira now explains how to enable JIT from its own Enable JIT button instead. (#109) - When a session can't start, Madeira now says why. (#109) - Games with a shared data section that isn't aligned to the iPhone's 16 KB memory pages now load. (#110) - Small 64-bit games built without relocation data now start. (#111) - The user profile's `AppData\LocalLow` folder now exists. Games and Steam components that keep files there work, and some no longer crash at start. ## beta 0.2.3 the per-game core settings translated into every language the app speaks, and two texts that were confidently telling people the wrong thing. ### Language - **The per-game core settings are readable in all fourteen languages.** The explanations under LLVM precompilation, SPU block size, resolution scale and the decoder mix existed only in English and Spanish, which meant that everyone else was choosing between values whose consequences were not written down anywhere they could read. Those, the two memory warnings, the settings notebook and the "this device cannot emulate" notice are now translated: 240 strings across the twelve remaining languages. What is still identical to English after this pass is the set of words that are the same word in that language — *Mono*, *Auto*, *Normal*, *Panel*, *Version* in German, *Options* in French — and changing those would only make them worse. ### Text - **The memory warning no longer promises that 8 GB of RAM is enough.** It ended by saying that devices with 8 GB or more need none of this, which is false and was reported by someone holding a phone with 12 GB who had just been blocked by it. The extended virtual addressing entitlement governs address space, not physical memory; extra RAM does not widen it. The notice now says the outcome depends on how the app was installed, which is the part the reader can act on. - **The credits show the version you are actually running.** The version was a translatable string copied by hand into all fourteen language blocks, and it had been left at `beta.0.1` while beta.0.2 was being handed out — three releases

## beta 0.2.0 ### Emulation - **A cache-maintenance call no longer kills the thread that makes it.** `sys_icache_invalidate` touches memory to do its work, so a null pointer takes the caller down with a segfault at address 0. One of the two calls in the SPU recompiler's dispatch path sits on the common exit, where the patch-point pointer is legitimately null because nothing was rewritten. It was killing all five SPURS kernels one after another, which left the game's twelve PPU threads waiting on them forever. From the outside it looked exactly like a hang: no error, CPU at 16 %, millions of idle sleeps. Fixed at the call site, and `psx3ios_jit_flush` now refuses an invalid address and records it instead of dying. - **The graphics layer is back to a state that draws.** A merge from another ARM64 port had left 28 files of the RSX and Vulkan code changed, among them the swapchain, the image-layout transitions and the pipeline compiler. The result was a game that ran perfectly and displayed nothing — broken geometry or a black screen — which is a hard symptom to read, because the emulator looks healthy: it compiles shaders, counts frames and uses CPU. Two additions that had no business in an iOS app went with it: an Android Vulkan loader and a profiler's GPU timer. - **x18 is always reserved on Apple hardware.** It is the platform register and the system may overwrite it at any moment, but LLVM only infers that from the target triple, and ours deliberately says `linux` so that its runtime linker emits ELF and builds the branch islands a 266 MiB code arena needs. It is now reserved in the backend itself, where no chain of options can leave it open, and every launch records whether it took effect. ### Settings - **Your settings now win over the recommended database.** Turning something off for a game was being silently undone at boot: the emulator applies its recommended per-game configuration after everything else, so the database overwrote the user's own choice with no indication anywhere. The recommended values still fill in what you have not touched, but the keys you set for that game are removed from them before they are applied, and the log says how many were dropped. - **The recommended database can be switched off entirely**, and ships off, so a game starts with your settings and nothing else ### Setup - **The guided setup finishes the job.** Everything under Settings → JIT can now be completed without leaving it: enabling JIT, choosing the StikDebug script, and turning on the launch handoff, alongside firmware and the memory entitlements — seven steps instead of five. Each action button shows the real state rather than an instruction, so "JIT enabled" and a script's filename tell you there is nothing left to do on that page. - **Installing firmware no longer closes the setup screen.** It used to dismiss itself so the library could do the work, which dropped the user out halfway through configuration with the distinct impression they had broken something. The file picker is now presented over the guide and the install runs inside it, spinner and all, returning to the same card with the button reading "Firmware installed". ### Interface - **The background colour can be changed**, in Settings → Theme. It tints the gradient, the waves and the specks without touching the theme itself: the two are separate on purpose, since wanting a different colour is not a reason to be given a different layout. Six to choose from, all dark enough to keep what sits on top readable. - **Everything decorative stops while a game runs.** The waves and the specks kept animating behind a game that covered them completely — GPU and battery taken from the emulation to draw something nobody can see. They now suspend when a game starts and resume when you leave it, and coming back from the background does not restart them while a game is still running. # DukeX v1.0.2 - Expanding the Xbox Experience DukeX v1.0.2 is our biggest step yet toward preserving the full original Xbox experience, not just the games. This release introduces the first native macOS build, expands XB.Live integration, and brings richer community features to both iOS and macOS. ## What's New - Native macOS release: DukeX is now available as a Mac Catalyst desktop build packaged with a nested Xemu fork, pairing desktop Xemu compatibility with the DukeX interface. - XB.Live Rich Presence and playtime tracking: friends can see what you are playing while DukeX tracks supported playtime sessions. - XB.Live messaging: threaded conversations, friend messaging, unread indicators, supported game invites, and existing Xbox inbox support now live inside DukeX. - XB.Live social expansion: friend requests, friend management, online presence, and deeper community integration are available from the Profile experience. - Activity Feed: XB.Live news, friend online status, friend achievement unlocks, and community updates now appear in a continuously refreshed timeline. - Controller Landscape Mode: on iOS, compatible controllers can switch DukeX into a controller-first browsing and launch experience. - Expanded AirPlay and external display support: big-screen play is more reliable across supported display configurations. ## Improvements - Improved achievements with Games, Apps, and Cores grouping plus updated artwork handling for XB.Live Core, DukeX Core, and special test titles. - Improved game tile spacing and cover handling across iOS and macOS. - Improved XB.Live cloud-save sync metadata with console identity v2, content-hash dedupe, and server-assisted cross-console restore handling. - Fixed achievement progress rounding so time-based achievements do not show 100% before they are actually complete. ## Availability - iOS: install `DukeX.v1.0.2.ipa` through StikStore, SideStore, or another supported sideloading workflow. - macOS: install `DukeX.macOS.v1.0.2.dmg` by dragging DukeX to Applications. - Hardware requirements on iOS remain Apple A14 Bionic or Apple M1 hardware or newer. - iOS 16.0 or later is supported, with iOS 16 support remaining experimental. ## Important DukeX does not include Xbox system files, game images, BIOS files, copyrighted content, signing certificates, or user games. Users must provide their own legally obtained files. DukeX is intended for legitimate emulation, preservation, testing, and personal library use.

On iOS 26 or later, use StikDebug with Universal.js assigned to DukeX. - If Auto Enable StikDebug is enabled, close StikDebug before launching a game from DukeX. - For Insignia testing, Force NAT to Insignia should remain enabled and the dashboard/account still need to be registered through Insignia's normal process. ## Known Issues - This is alpha software and title compatibility varies heavily by game, device, thermal state, and JIT availability. - Some rendering issues remain, including known HUD/depth/primitive artifacts in certain titles. - Apple's Metal HUD may still not appear even when requested; use the built-in DukeX stats HUD for basic device-side readings. - Gameplay performance may vary between cutscenes, menus, and active gameplay. - The app is not intended for use with pirated materials. ## Build Details - Bundle ID: `com.mafty.dukex` - Version: `0.1.2` - Build: `12` - Target: iPhoneOS arm64 - Release type: unsigned alpha IPA

# DukeX v1.0.2 - Expanding the Xbox Experience

DukeX v1.0.2 is our biggest step yet toward preserving the full original Xbox
experience, not just the games. This release introduces the first native macOS
build, expands XB.Live integration, and brings richer community features to both
iOS and macOS.

## What's New

- Native macOS release: DukeX is now available as a Mac Catalyst desktop build
  packaged with a nested Xemu fork, pairing desktop Xemu compatibility with the
  DukeX interface.
- XB.Live Rich Presence and playtime tracking: friends can see what you are
  playing while DukeX tracks supported playtime sessions.
- XB.Live messaging: threaded conversations, friend messaging, unread
  indicators, supported game invites, and existing Xbox inbox support now live
  inside DukeX.
- XB.Live social expansion: friend requests, friend management, online presence,
  and deeper community integration are available from the Profile experience.
- Activity Feed: XB.Live news, friend online status, friend achievement unlocks,
  and community updates now appear in a continuously refreshed timeline.
- Controller Landscape Mode: on iOS, compatible controllers can switch DukeX
  into a controller-first browsing and launch experience.
- Expanded AirPlay and external display support: big-screen play is more
  reliable across supported display configurations.

## Improvements

- Improved achievements with Games, Apps, and Cores grouping plus updated
  artwork handling for XB.Live Core, DukeX Core, and special test titles.
- Improved game tile spacing and cover handling across iOS and macOS.
- Improved XB.Live cloud-save sync metadata with console identity v2,
  content-hash dedupe, and server-assisted cross-console restore handling.
- Fixed achievement progress rounding so time-based achievements do not show
  100% before they are actually complete.

## Availability

- iOS: install `DukeX.v1.0.2.ipa` through StikStore, SideStore, or another
  supported sideloading workflow.
- macOS: install `DukeX.macOS.v1.0.2.dmg` by dragging DukeX to Applications.
- Hardware requirements on iOS remain Apple A14 Bionic or Apple M1 hardware or
  newer.
- iOS 16.0 or later is supported, with iOS 16 support remaining experimental.

## Important

DukeX does not include Xbox system files, game images, BIOS files, copyrighted
content, signing certificates, or user games. Users must provide their own
legally obtained files. DukeX is intended for legitimate emulation,
preservation, testing, and personal library use.

# Iridium 0.2.0 Download your Steam games directly in Iridium, manage repairs and updates, and try the updated Windows runtime. Game support remains experimental. ## Download **[Download Iridium (.ipa)](https://github.com/intraducine/iridium/releases/download/v0.2.0/Iridium-unsigned.ipa)** Requires **iOS or iPadOS 18+**, JIT, and games you own. You only need the IPA to install; supply your own game files or download owned games from Steam. ## Install 1. Sign and install the IPA and helper with a compatible sideloading tool, or import it into LiveContainer using its supported JIT setup. 2. Open Iridium and configure JIT in **Launch Support**. 3. Open **Downloads → Steam** to sign in and queue a game, or use **Add Game** to import a game folder. Choose its executable, add it to your library, then press **Play**. For standalone installation, preserve `com.apple.developer.kernel.increased-memory-limit=true` in both Iridium's final app signature and provisioning profile. The anonymous ad-hoc carrier alone grants no installation or memory rights. In LiveContainer, the container process's signature, profile, and JIT setup determine effective rights; importing the guest IPA does not grant them. Both routes still need device validation. Back up your saves before updating. Update the existing app or LiveContainer entry without deleting its data. Steam repairs and updates keep older installations; saves stored inside an older game folder may need to be copied manually to the new one. # Iridium 0.2.0

Download your Steam games directly in Iridium, manage repairs and updates, and try the updated Windows runtime. Game support remains experimental.

## Download

**[Download Iridium (.ipa)](https://github.com/intraducine/iridium/releases/download/v0.2.0/Iridium-unsigned.ipa)**

Requires **iOS or iPadOS 18+**, JIT, and games you own. You only need the IPA to install; supply your own game files or download owned games from Steam.

## Install

1. Sign and install the IPA and helper with a compatible sideloading tool, or import it into LiveContainer using its supported JIT setup.
2. Open Iridium and configure JIT in **Launch Support**.
3. Open **Downloads → Steam** to sign in and queue a game, or use **Add Game** to import a game folder. Choose its executable, add it to your library, then press **Play**.

For standalone installation, preserve `com.apple.developer.kernel.increased-memory-limit=true` in both Iridium's final app signature and provisioning profile. The anonymous ad-hoc carrier alone grants no installation or memory rights. In LiveContainer, the container process's signature, profile, and JIT setup determine effective rights; importing the guest IPA does not grant them. Both routes still need device validation.

Back up your saves before updating. Update the existing app or LiveContainer entry without deleting its data. Steam repairs and updates keep older installations; saves stored inside an older game folder may need to be copied manually to the new one. Keep that older folder until you have checked your saves.

## What's new

- **Steam downloads in the app.** Sign in with a password or QR code, with Steam Guard support, browse your library, and choose download language, unprotected branch, 32/64-bit files, and owned DLC.
- **A download queue with verification and repair.** Pause, resume, retry, and prioritize downloads. Check for updates or repair downloaded files while keeping the previous installation.
- **Clearer storage warnings.** Download checks use the space available to Iridium and account for verified partial files. **Download Anyway** can bypass an estimated-space warning for one attempt; file verification and real out-of-space errors remain enforced.
- **Updated Windows runtime.** Includes 32-bit WoW64 support and D3D9/D3D12 updates. Support still varies by game and device.
- **Game prerequisite installers.** Run supported setup steps included with a game, or choose **Game Options → Run Installer** for an EXE or MSI installer you provide. Some installers need interaction. Closing the player requests cancellation; Iridium keeps observing the runtime's exit and reports when a restart is required.
- **Reduced duplicate runtime data.** Identical Windows runtime files share one packaged copy. The main app's anonymous ad-hoc signature carries only the increased-memory-limit request; helpers remain unsigned until you sign them.

## Known issues

- Physical-device compatibility for these changes has not been established. Some games may fail to launch or have graphics, video, audio, input, save, or shutdown problems. Skyrim speech and mouse attack issues remain unverified.
- Keep Iridium open while downloading. Downloads pause when the app goes into the background and need to be resumed. Real-account downloads and recovery after Wi-Fi or network loss still need device testing.
- Steam Cloud, Workshop, Steam Families library discovery, password-protected branches, and desktop Steam services are not included. Games that require Steamworks/DRM, anti-cheat, or other unsupported runtime features may not launch after downloading.
- Updates keep older game copies and need extra storage. **Download Anyway** does not create free space; exhausting device storage can also prevent other apps from saving.
- JIT and available memory depend on your device and signing setup; LiveContainer and standalone results can differ. Built-in JIT requires standalone Iridium, debugging permission, a valid pairing file, and LocalDevVPN. Hosted Iridium uses external JIT. Recipient signing, LiveContainer hosting, and game prerequisite success still need device testing.

versions.localizedDescription: # LiveContainer 3.8.0 > [!Warning] > The standalone version requires **SideStore 0.6.2+** or **AltStore 2.2.1+** for installation. > To install LiveContainer with built-in SideStore (`LiveContainer+SideStore.ipa`), please use [Impactor](https://github.com/khcrysalis/Impactor) or [iloader](https://github.com/nab138/iloader). See [our installation guide](https://livecontainer.github.io/docs/installation/lc_sidestore) for details. # New Features ## Storage Management - Added a new storage management view with a breakdown of app bundles, containers, temporary files, app group data, tweaks, and other files. (Hidden apps' size is included in "other" section until unlocked) - Added per-app storage details, including app bundle size, container sizes, and last-used date. - Added actions to clean temporary files and caches, including guest app caches and LiveContainer's own caches. ## Multiple LiveContainers - Added configurable launch priority for multiple LiveContainer instances, making shared-app shortcuts choose available instances in the order you prefer. (#1367) ## Share to Apps in LiveContainer Added a share extension to LiveContainer. When you share a URL or a file from iOS's share sheet, LiveContainer will ask which app you would like to open the URL/file in, so the old share to LiveContainer shortcut method is no longer needed. When an ipa file is shared in this way, LiveContainer will ask if you want to install it in LiveContainer or in the built-in SideStore (if installed) (#1357) ## Multitasking - Added per-app multitask preferences. Each app can now follow the global setting, always launch in multitask mode, or avoid multitask mode. (#1208) - Improved multitask dock behavior: the dock can be made smaller, hidden more cleanly, and has improved padding. (#1228, #1250) - Added more multitask window animations and improved native-window scene handling. - URL schemes and `open-url` payloads can be passed to already-running multitask apps and native windows. ## JIT - Added StosDebug support as a JIT enabler. ## TweakLoader You can now disable tweaks in the "Tweaks" page in LiveContainer's UI. by @SAOMDVN # Improvements - Added support for manually setting a container's IDFV. (#1194) - IDFV spoofing works even when Tweakloader is not loaded. - Reworked signing logic for tweaks and app installation, with multithreaded signing support. - Download alerts now block tab switching while a download is in progress. - Crash reports are shown in a sheet instead of a large alert for better performance on newer iOS versions. - Add a "Clear Notification" button (#1388) - Added some popular NSBonjourServices keys so apps can discover AirPlay devices and remote pairing pairable hosts in the local network. (#1417) # Bug Fixes - Fixed `livecontainer://open-url` dropping the deep link when launching an app from a cold start. (#1339) - Fixed the Add to Home Screen menu failing or behaving incorrectly by replacing the SwiftUI context menu implementation. (#1209) - Fixed a crash when opening Container Preferences if the app did not contain an `en.lproj` path. (#1239) - Fixed apps and AltStore sources not being searchable in some cases. (#1365, #1368) - Fixed converting a shared app back to private after aborting an install with the same bundle identifier, which could leave stale container state behind. (#1347) - Fixed shortcuts and JIT flows getting stuck on a busy LiveContainer instance instead of using another available instance. (#1386) - Fixed file picker not workings for some apps because Tweakloader is not loaded after enabling "Hide LiveContainer from dyld API". (#1430) - Fixed several app launch compatibility issues on iOS 26.5 beta, and some multitask/JIT app launches. (#1300, #1310, #1329) - Fixed multitask keyboard focus issues on iOS 17.4+, including cases where the keyboard would not appear, Passwords would immediately close, or video playback would freeze in multitask mode. (#1402, #844, #870) - Added support for iOS 27 developer beta.

For more information, please see [3.7.0 release note](https://github.com/LiveContainer/LiveContainer/releases/tag/3.7.0). ## Bug Fixes - Fix an issue where built-in SideStore may freeze on launch (#1158) - Fix the ipa of another LiveContainer not generating in LiveContainer+SideStore builds after SideStore's massive codebase change (#1184) - Fix the new Launch App Shortcut does not work below iOS 18 (#1159) - The Launch App Shortcut now reports meaningful errors - Fix crash when using external container in multitasking mode - Fix process hangs when debugging multitask private apps ## New Features - The "Tap top of the view to scroll to top" action can be passed through to multitasking guest apps.

# LiveContainer 3.7.0 > [!Warning] > The standalone version requires **SideStore 0.6.2+** or **AltStore 2.2.1+** for installation. > We recommend installing LiveContainer + SideStore using [Impactor](https://github.com/khcrysalis/Impactor) or [iloader](https://github.com/nab138/iloader). See [our installation guide](https://livecontainer.github.io/docs/installation/lc_sidestore) for details. Happy Spring Festival / Lunar New Year! After six months of development, we’re excited to release **LiveContainer 3.7.0**. This update introduces several powerful new features, including the Launch App Shortcut, iOS 26 JIT script support, external containers, native icon generation, and more. # New Features ## Launch App Shortcut > [!Note] > This feature requires LiveContainer to be installed with at least the **LaunchAppExtension** and **LaunchAppExtensionHelper** extension. iOS 16+ is supported. A new extension allows apps to launch instantly without opening the LiveContainer main interface (for apps that are not locked, hidden, or JIT-required). Once configured, the shortcut prepares the runtime environment and selects an available LiveContainer instance to launch the app directly. This reduces extra relaunches and jumps and typically saves 1~2 seconds per launch. See the [setup guide](https://livecontainer.github.io/docs/guides/add-to-home-screen) for instructions. ## JIT Support for iOS 26 JIT scripts has been added by @Vishram1123. Scripts can be configured in app-specific settings and loaded automatically on iOS 26+. The **“StikDebug in another LiveContainer”** option has been fixed, allowing StikDebug to run within LiveContainer. When launching a JIT-required app, LiveContainer will automatically detect StikDebug, launch it in an available container, and pass all required parameters — including scripts — to enable JIT. In addition, when enabling JIT for multitasked app, LiveContainer will prioritize launching StikDebug as a multitask app to save app slot usage. (TODO: this doesn’t automatically minimize StikDebug after enabling JIT, might be added later) Be sure to convert StikDebug into a shared app before use. ## External Containers > [!Note] > Containers stored on external media (portable drives, SMB shares, etc.) are unsupported by many apps and may cause instability or crashes. You can now use external folders as app containers. This is useful if you want to manage app data through a file manager while still accessing it in LiveContainer, or if you want maintain container access when an app is shared. To configure this, open: **App-Specific Settings → Select External Data Folder** ## Native Icons LiveContainer now generates icons using native iOS libraries. On iOS 18+, this enables proper Light, Dark, and Original (Liquid Glass) icon rendering. These icons can also be saved for home screen shortcuts. ## Multitasking Improvements * Added **“Skip app terminate screen”** (by @boa-z) * Added **”Single Window Mode”** to minimize other apps when a maximized app is brought to front * Launch URL schemes can now be passed to multitasking apps. Passing URL between multitask apps can be controlled via **”Redirect URL to Host”** switch * Launching Private Apps is now possible. By default, apps launched with private container is only given sandbox access to its own data container folder. You can change it in developer settings. * Changed animations a little bit ## AltStore Source Support Basic AltSource support has been implemented by @StephenDev0. Sources can be added using: ``` livecontainer://sources?url=<URL> ``` ## Other Additions * App remarks are now supported (by @WingCH) * Decrypted apps can now be installed via `itms-services` links (by @WingCH) # Bug Fixes * Fixed iOS 26.4b1 compatibility (#1152) * Fixed crashes caused by `-[NSUserDefaults synchronize]` returning NO * Fixed signing crashes when apps contain too many libraries (#1135) * Fixed signing failure when not enough space is available to insert HM_DYLIB in Mach-O headers

# ⚠️This version ⚠️REQUIRES⚠️ SideStore 0.6.2+ / AltStore 2.2.1+ to install. >[!Note] > This a minor release that solves the following issues in version 3.6.0 and adds the following features. For more information, please see [3.6.0 release note](https://github.com/LiveContainer/LiveContainer/releases/tag/3.6.0). - Fixed an issue where symbol offset caches were not reset after an iOS update, causing crashes. Fixes #765 #757 #760 - Fixed a bug where window controls could appear behind the status bar if the app was terminated while in full-screen mode with the dock hidden. Fixes #742 - Fixed an issue preventing the built-in SideStore from deactivating apps. Fixes #725 - Fixed a problem where LiveContainer failed to locate certain symbols in dyld on iPad 7 running iOS 18.6. Fixes #746 - Fixed a crash that could occur when LiveContainer attempted to check if another instance of LiveContainer was running. Fixes #751 - Fixed an issue where LiveContainer tries to open private app in another LiveContainer if an app is running in the primary LiveContainer. # New Features - On iPad, LiveContainer will now only open a new window in full-screen mode if LiveContainer itself is already in full-screen mode. - The "Fix File Picker and Local Notifications" option has been split into three separate options: **Fix File Picker**, **Fix Local Notifications**, and **Use LiveContainer's Bundle ID**. Implements #739 # Localization - Updated translations: Arabic, Japanese, Polish, and Brazilian Portuguese. - Added Korean translation, contributed by @Dr-Sauce.

# ⚠️This version ⚠️REQUIRES⚠️ SideStore 0.6.2+ / AltStore 2.2.1+ to install. >[!Note] > Yes, as heralded in the 3.5.0 release, and due to the removal of Store patching, SideStore 0.6.2+ / AltStore 2.2.1+ is required to install this version of LiveContainer. You can use "Import/Refresh Certificate from AltStore/SideStore" button to setup JIT-Less mode. This version of LiveContainer focuses on quality-of-life improvements, new features such as app sorting and enhanced multitasking, as well as various bug fixes. # New Features ## New Icon 1. LiveContainer/LiveContainer2 now has a new HD icon and supports dark and tinted modes. By @m1337v. ## Multitasking 1. A dock has been added for multitasking mode. The dock can be hidden by dragging it to the edge of the screen, and collapsed by tapping the collapse button. You can also resize the dock in the settings. By @boa-z. 2. In windowed multitasking mode, you can now maximize or minimize windows using buttons on the new window bar. By @boa-z. 3. When maximized, the window will occupy the safe area. Additionally, if the dock is collapsed, the entire window bar will be hidden, allowing the app to take up the full screen. 4. You can now place the window bar at the bottom of the window. 5. Windows will now automatically resize when the device is rotated. 6. You can now choose whether to automatically exit Picture-in-Picture (PiP) mode when returning to LiveContainer. This option is available in the LiveContainer settings. 7. The window hosting PiP is now automatically hidden, and is restored when dismissing PiP. ## App Management 1. You can now double-tap an app to quickly open its settings. By @m1337v. 2. Apps can now be sorted by name (A–Z, Z–A), last opened date, installation date, or a custom order, allowing you to arrange them however you like. By @boa-z and @m1337v. 3. You can now view an app's installation date and last launch date in its settings. ## [EXPERIMENTAL] Built-in SideStore This experimental feature combines both LiveContainer and SideStore into a single app, saving one app slot for other standalone apps. You can try it out by downloading "LiveContainer+SideStore.ipa". Currently, SideStore itself, the refresh shortcut, and the widget are functional. See here for all changes made to original SideStore https://github.com/hugeBlack/SideStore/tree/LiveContainerSupport > [!Note] > LiveProcess is required to use the refresh shortcut. > It has been reported that the built-in SideStore cannot determine the device UDID if the standalone SideStore is running in the background. New Re-Sign Strategy Instead of keeping track of expiration date, LiveContainer now directly ask iOS to determine whether the code signature is valid, which significantly decreases app re-sign rate. PancakeStore is officially EoL (End-of-Life) as of 8/22/2026.

Apple has implemented server-side changes to the iTunes API that's used in PancakeStore, as well as other popular tools such as ipatool, which primarily include SEP-based device attestation. What this means, in short, is that PancakeStore will not work ever again unless someone figures out an alternative route for downgrading apps, or successfully re-implements the attestation logic (both of which are very difficult).

In the event that this occurs, or a new method for downgrading apps is discovered and made, we will update PancakeStore.
Until then, consider the project EoL.

Thank you all for all of your support of this tool, and we apologize that things have to halt like this.
